LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 8 picks, including the Bills to top the Ravens in a high-scoring game Imagn Images Going to the dogs last week turned out to be dog doodoo. I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going. Pick: Packers 31, Panthers 24 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. Pick: Seahawks 24, Bears 17 Now Playing Share Share Video Prisco's Week 8 picks: Packers over Panthers, Lions beat Vikings Bills win Super Bowl? Cowboys take NFC East? LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. home.headline: Green Bay Packers: Micah Parsons sounds off on NFL officials following team’s Week 7 loss to Lions
home.blurb: Josh Jacobs says he is remorseful in first comments since Packers return Green Bay Packers: Micah Parsons sounds off on NFL officials following team’s Week 7 loss to Lions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Milwaukee can finally celebrate Jokić's 200th triple-double Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Green Bay Packers fell to the Detroit Lions on Sunday afternoon by the score of 20-17. Unfortunately, issues that have plagued the team all year, such as injuries, dropped passes, and missed kicks, reared their ugly heads again in Week Seven. Indeed, had the Packers played fundamental and mistake-free football, they would have won the game. After all, the Lions needed a field goal in the closing seconds of the contest in order to win. After the game was over, though, a great deal of criticism was directed at the NFL officials who refereed the game, including by one Packers player who was not able to participate: Micah Parsons . Green Bay Packers star Micah Parsons criticizes NFL officials Green Bay Packers defensive end Micah Parsons (1) celebrates his sack during the fourth quarter of their game Sunday, September 7, 2025 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. The Green Bay Packers beat the Detroit Lions 27-13. For their part, the Packers players themselves are not making excuses for the loss. That is, they are not at all saying that the reason they lost in Detroit was because of the officials. However, they are frustrated with the confusing calls made against them. Multiple players expressed their frustration about bogus roughing the passer calls while Jordan Love was mugged without any flags being thrown. They just want the game called fairly. Parsons, for his part, posted the following message on social media: This particular post is a reference, specifically, to how Brenton Cox was literally pushed into Lions quarterback Jared Goff and whistled for roughing the passer. Over the last several weeks, Green Bay players have been called for this penalty just for putting their hands on an opposing quarterback. At some point, something is going to have to change regarding how the officials are calling Packers games. Even the national media, including Tom Brady, thought the games was terrible in terms of how one-sided the referees were. The Packers won the game, 27-13. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. And as Dajani said, this Minnesota offense just does not have the ability to get into a high-scoring game and come away with a win. They need the defense to hold the opponent down entirely, and I'm not sure that even Flores' bunch can do that in the friendly confines of Ford Field. … Prediction: Lions 23, Vikings 14 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) Dajani (Steelers -3.5): How can the Browns keep getting away with this? They overcame a 14-0 deficit in Nashville on Sunday, as Harold Fannin Jr . took a short reception 36 yards down the field with 20 seconds remaining to set up a 32-yard game-winning field goal from Andre Szmyt . Deshaun Watson became the third quarterback since 1970 to register a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of the season. With this being a divisional game against an opponent that just got back from Paris, I can understand why some would take the points with the underdog given the hook. But the Steelers are 3-0 ATS at home. That includes Week 3, when they dropped 30 points on Joe Burrow and the Bengals in a win, and Week 5, when Pittsburgh scored 34 points in a double-digit victory over the Colts. The Steelers are averaging 26.0 points per game over their last five contests, which ranks top 10 in the NFL, and are 8-0 SU and ATS in their last eight home games vs. the Browns. In fact, Pittsburgh is actually a perfect 11-0 ATS in its last 11 home divisional games. Insane stat. … Prediction: Steelers 26, Browns 21 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): I don't understand how the Browns keep doing it. Every single one of their victories has required a game-winning drive in the final five minutes of the game. That's not sustainable on any level whatsoever. The Steelers don't exactly have consistency written all over them, considering the vagaries of their passing game and the fact that their three-game winning streak has come against weak opponents. However, I trust Jaylen Warren and Co. more than I do the Browns at this point. … Prediction: Steelers 20, Browns 13 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) Dajani (Falcons +2.5): I have plenty of questions about both of these teams, but I did tell you the Falcons were going to cover the small number vs. the 49ers last week! Atlanta finished that game on a 26-6 run after trailing 14-3. They scored on four straight drives. I'm not sure the Buccaneers deserve to be three-point favorites this week after that destruction of the Panthers. Baker Mayfield had to throw for just 64 yards and a touchdown in a 43-13 victory, as Bucky Irving , Kenneth Gainwell and Sean Tucker combined for 246 yards rushing and three touchdowns. This Falcons rush defense ranks fourth in the NFL with 88.9 rushing yards allowed per game. Plus, the Falcons have won two road games this season by 20+ points after being listed as an underdog, and are 4-0 ATS in their last four road games against the Buccaneers. … Prediction: Falcons 26, Buccaneers 24 Dubin (Falcons +2.5): The Buccaneers ran all over the Panthers last week, but Atlanta has actually been quite good against the run, allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season. Can Tampa really control the game with Bucky Irving the way it did last week, or will it have to actually turn Baker Mayfield loose as a passer here? If the Bucs have to do that, I have more confidence in Atlanta's offense right now, with Bijan Robinson , Drake London and even Kyle Pitts contributing at a high level. … Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 17 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Dajani ( Broncos +1.5): The Broncos had an embarrassing outing last time they played the Chiefs, allowing 247 yards off of 28 missed tackles in a 31-10 loss. There has been a lot of talk about Bo Nix and the offense, but what about the Chiefs? They averaged 4.3 yards per play and recorded just 213 yards of total offense in that embarrassing loss to the Seahawks. The team seemingly never got off the bus. Jackson returned to practice ahead of Week 7 against the Cincinnati Bengals, and he was officially listed as questionable for that matchup before eventually being ruled out. With a huge matchup against the Buffalo Bills coming up in Week 8, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter provided an update on Jackson's status on Monday. On optimism level for Lamar Jackson, Minter said, "Lamar is working his butt off to be out there. He'll be in a decent spot, but we'll know more on Wednesday." It seems like Jackson has a chance to make his return in Week 8, and the odds at DraftKings reflect that. Baltimore opened -- and remains -- a 3.5-point underdog in this AFC showdown, and it likely would be closer to a touchdown underdog if backup Tyler Huntley has to start. This is a huge game for the Ravens in the AFC playoff picture, as they've fallen to 4-3 and are in last place in the AFC North. All four teams in the AFC North are over .500, leaving very little room for erro for Baltimore if it wants to make the playoffs. The Bills are one of the toughest opponents left on the team's schedule, as they enter this game with a 5-1 record. While Huntley has not played terribly in place of Jackson, the Ravens are now 1-2 in his three starts this season. All-time, the Ravens have won just seven of the 20 games that Jackson has missed in his career. So, there's no doubt that this line would move in favor of Buffalo if the two-time MVP is unable to go. Minter seems to be pushing any Lamar speculation until after the team's practice on Wednesday, though it was reported on Sunday that the star quarterback is "confident" he'll be on the field in Week 8. In his four games this season, Jackson completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six scores and just one interception. He also has 19 carries for 144 yards and a score. He ended up sitting in Week 7 after being limited in what he could do running the ball. Jackson may need a full practice this week to suit up against Buffalo in what could be the marquee matchup of Sunday's slate . Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. The Baltimore Ravens are trending toward getting Lamar Jackson back for Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Buffalo Bills. Jackson has missed each of the team's last three games after suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 4. The Ravens are 1-2 over that stretch, losing each of their last two matchups against the division-rival Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals. On Wednesday, Jackson started the week of practice with full participation. Given his full participation early in the week, it appears Jackson will be good to go this coming Sunday — barring any injury setbacks. The Ravens began their 2026 campaign with a 4-1 start, but have since dropped to 4-3. away.headline: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson expected to play in Week 8: report
away.blurb: Jackson was able to notch limited practice participation leading up to this past Sunday’s Week 7 loss to the Bengals, but he was ultimately ruled out. Now, the Ravens are gearing up for a highly-anticipated Week 8 matchup against the Buffalo Bills. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has missed each of the last three games after suffering an ankle injury in Week 4. The Ravens are 1-2 over that span with Tyler Huntley at the helm, dropping each of their last two games against the division-rival Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals. On Tuesday, NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport confidently reported that Jackson will be on the field for this Week 8 clash. “I expect, based on the people that I’ve spoken with, that Lamar Jackson will play this week. He will be on the field this week against the Buffalo Bills,” Rapoport said. “I know we’ve been here before. This was a 2-3 week injury — he’s through the third week. He is believed to be as close to 100% as he has been and the Ravens do expect him to play.” With Jackson off the field, the Ravens have dropped to last place in the AFC North standings with a 4-3 record. They’ll look to get back in the win column in a difficult road matchup against the Bills this coming Sunday. Sunday’s game will kick off at 1 p.m. ET. The Ravens then have a short week to prepare for a “Thursday Night Football” matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 9. home.headline: Bills injury report: Spencer Brown sits, Tyrell Shavers returns
home.blurb: Brown getting the benefit of a bye week to rest the back injury he assured us was just some soreness and something he tweaked after a long plane ride out west, may not have been enough. Now he is saying he rested through practice in Week 6 so he would be available when the Bills faced the Las Vegas Raiders. He is still sore, still resting – three weeks later. Bills players with limited practice: Moore and Oliver being limited rather than non-participants is encouraging. Sure, it would have been nice to think a week of no football would heal them, but realistically, we may see them on this list all year. So, limited to start the week is a positive. The Buffalo Bills got back to work on Wednesday. The hope has widely been that the bye week would give some added rest to players who had been nursing bumps, bruises, and those injuries that were keeping them from going full speed. While we see one name returning for the first time this season, an extra week of rest may not have been enough for another. _____________________________________________________________________________ OLB Bradley Chubb (chest/thumb) WR Tyrell Shavers – PUP – (knee) There’s plenty of good news in this group. Buffalo opened the 21-day practice window on Shavers. The wide receiver had ACL surgery in late January. He now has until the week before Thanksgiving to get back on the roster. Alford hasn’t healed and Chubb, who noticeably missed some snaps in Week 6, added a chest injury to his list of ailments. The bigger concern is Dalton Kincaid. Especially after last week’s blown two-score lead to the Cleveland Browns, nobody is expecting Robert Saleh’s first team in Nashville to execute a miraculous turnaround. Draft discussions are already becoming relevant, if that tells you anything. Still, the Titans hit the road to face the Cincinnati Bengals this coming Sunday, and it’s a chance for Tennessee to win their second game in three weeks. That’s somehow still an exciting prospect. To preview the matchup, I’ve got one reason the Titans will beat the Bengals, one reason they won’t, and my own prediction for what will actually happen. Let’s start with the former. Will: Titans’ secondary sees massive uptick Two weeks in a row now, Tennessee has forced at least one interception. The Titans have come down with three picks over the last two games, two of which belong to rising offseason pickup Cor’Dale Flott. Tennessee Titans cornerback Cor'dale Flott (18) intercepts Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) on Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. Tennessee is facing one of the best pass-first teams in the NFL. If Saleh's secondary can find consistency beyond the occasional turnover, the Titans would have more than a fair chance to shut down RB Chase Brown on the ground, too. It's much easier to stop Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins in concept than it is on the field, but doing so is the Titans' key to winning this one. Won’t: Titans can't overcome inconsistent Bengals defense The inverse, of course, is if the Titans' offense continues to suffer. The Bengals have proved themselves beatable against "bad" teams - just see their narrow, one-score win over the 1-6 Miami Dolphins two weeks ago. But Cincinnati also just dismantled the Baltimore Ravens last week, 35-13. The through line is that Cincy scored 30+ points in both of those contests; it comes down to the opposing offense's ability to hang in there when Burrow and his crew get hot. Tennessee ranks 31st in both touchdowns and points per game. Almost everywhere the Bengals are in the top 10 through the air, the Titans are in the bottom 10. Cincy has allowed 20+ points in four of their six games this season. If Cam Ward can get back on his feet in any sense of the saying, another 24-point performance like Tennessee had last week could be enough to at least make this one interesting. However, the Titans may need a little more juice than they've seen yet this season from their QB to stay in it. Prediction: Titans lose, 31-20 Ultimately, I have the Titans falling to 1-7 in this one. We've seen a number of trends solidify that this roster has failed to prove their ability to rise beyond. Carnell Tate is the primary receiver in an otherwise underwhelming offense. The defense can force early turnovers, but can't get late stops when it matters - especially when it comes to tackling. Ward has a better second half than his typically abysmal first, but by the time Tennessee tries to get aggressive, it's too late to make a difference. I expect most of, if not all of these notes to be hit in Week 8. I don't think the Titans will lose in a blowout, but on the road against one of the best offenses in the league, this one already looks like too much for Saleh's team. picks.blurb: 5 Cam Ward QB stats illustrate how he's developing with Tennessee Titans News Sports Counties Business Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals TITANS Titans scouting report vs Cincinnati Bengals, matchups, prediction NFL Week 8 Tyler Palmateer Nashville Tennessean Oct. 28, 2026, 5:04 a.m. CT The Tennessee Titans will face the Cincinnati Bengals in NFL Week 8 following a 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns. The Bengals' passing offense, led by quarterback Joe Burrow, poses a significant challenge to the Titans' struggling defense. Positives are hard to find amid the Tennessee Titans’ struggles, but running back Tony Pollard was one last week. The Memphis native had his second-best game as a Titans player, with 129 yards rushing and three touchdowns on 25 carries in a gutting 27-24 home loss to the Cleveland Browns on Oct. 25. Maybe Pollard can do it again when the Titans (1-6) face the Cincinnati Bengals (4-2) at Paycor Stadium on Nov. 1 (noon CT, CBS) in NFL Week 8. The Bengals' and Browns ' run defenses are about the same statistically. Cincinnati allows 116.3 rushing yards per game, which ranks 19th in the league. The Titans gained a season-high 322 yards of offense with Pollard’s contributions, taking pressure off developing second-year quarterback Cam Ward . Tennessee coach Robert Saleh pinned the Browns loss on defense . Now that unit will face Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow, who’s 11th in the league with 1,653 yards passing, and second with 15 passing touchdowns, to go with three interceptions. Here’s our scouting report for the Titans’ game against the Browns. One Cincinnati Bengals stat to know Cincinnati has 13 pass plays of 25 yards or more this season. Tennessee has seven. Where Tennessee Titans have edge vs. Bengals The good news: Cincinnati’s offense ranks 29th in rushing yards per game (81.2), so there’s an opportunity for the Titans to make the Bengals one-dimensional. The bad news: Cincinnati’s offense is doing fine without a rushing threat, averaging 345.2 yards. It isn’t a big Titans advantage, but they must capitalize on it and see if stopping the run allows their pass rush to play like it did against the Colts (six sacks). It will take a stark turnaround after Tennessee allowed a season-high 183 yards rushing against the Browns. That marked the franchise’s worst single-game Pro Football Focus run defense grade (36.3) since 2023. Personnel changes up front have not helped. Run-stopping defensive tackle Jordan Elliott was released on Oct. 20 after breaking the NFL's gun policy . Third-year defender Timmy Horne was signed from the practice squad to replace him. Where Cincinnati Bengals have edge vs. Titans Tennessee’s secondary tackled poorly and took bad angles against the Browns, making rookie receiver KC Concepcion look like a Pro Bowler (eight catches, 129 yards). Imagine what Burrow and receivers Tee Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase might do. The Titans haven't seen an offense like this in 2026. The Bengals are seventh in the league in passing yards per game (264) and get 76% of their total yards through the air. Higgins and Chase have accounted for nine of the Bengals’ 13 explosive pass plays. Saleh’s also soul-searching in his secondary. Alontae Taylor was signed in the offseason to fortify one of Tennessee’s outside corner spots, but he was made inactive in Week 6 by coach’s decision and didn’t see the field in Week 7. Now it looks like Taylor will likely move to nickel . This would be a good week for Taylor to make a contribution, assuming Saleh plays him. Score prediction: Bengals 35, Titans 21 The Titans' scarred defense won’t be able to slow Burrow, and they can’t depend on Ward to keep pace in a shootout. It looks like their worst-case scenario matchup. Winning the turnover battle and making a few plays on special teams would help, but the Titans will be fortunate to keep it within 14 points. The Cincinnati Bengals are coming off a monster win over the Baltimore Ravens , but they cannot afford to let that lead to them overlooking their next opponent, the Tennessee Titans. I know the Titans are 1-6 and are not a good football team. But this is the NFL, where the margin for error is razor-thin, if that. For the Bengals, this is a prime opportunity to squash any sense of this game being a trap game— coming off a dominant road win at Baltimore and going to Madrid in two weeks— and putting their first complete game together this season. Right now, on FanDuel , the Bengals are a 10.5-point favorite against the Titans. Their moneyline is -650, and the over/under is 46.5 points. This will be Tennessee’s first time playing in Cincinnati since 2020. Ironically, that was Week 8 in 2020 and on November 1st. The Bengals won that game 31-20, which was a coming-out party for Joe Burrow in his rookie season. Burrow was 26/37 for 249 yards and two touchdowns in that game, making a featured appearance on the highlights during NBC’s Sunday Night Football game coverage that night. Since that game, the Bengals and Titans have played four times in Nashville, including in the Divisional round of the 2021 NFL Playoffs. That was the game where Joe Burrow overcame nine sacks and willed the Bengals to a 19-16 win that was the first road playoff win in Bengals history. Cincinnati beat Tennessee 37-27 in Week 15 of the 2024 Season, which was the most recent matchup between the two teams. Tennessee’s head coach is Robert Saleh, in his first season with the Titans. He previously coached the New York Jets and served two stints as the San Francisco 49ers’ defensive coordinator. The Titans are 1-6 and coming off a last-second 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 7. Quarterback Cam Ward is in his second season and has thrown for just 1,179 yards and just four touchdowns this season. Ward also has just one game with over 200 passing yards. Entering Sunday, the Titans were in the bottom two in the NFL in both scoring and total offense, while ranking in the middle of the pack in both scoring and total defense. However, the Titans have been competitive most of the season, as four of their six losses came by one score. Two of them were to the division-leading Giants (12-7) and the aforementioned loss to Cleveland. away.headline: Jeremiyah Love injury: Arizona Cardinals RB expected to miss Week 7
away.blurb: Love did not practice all last week and did not play against the Los Angeles Rams . He was a non-participant in practice on Wednesday. It sounds like he will sit the rest of this week as well. On Wednesday, coach Mike LaFleur indicated the Cardinals are focused on getting him right. "He's feeling better, but it kind of goes without saying — (We're) not going to put him out there until he feels 100%." Jeremiyah Love injury: Arizona Cardinals RB expected to miss Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Milwaukee can finally celebrate Jokić's 200th triple-double Jeremiyah Love injury: Arizona Cardinals RB expected to miss Week 7 Jess Root, Cardinals Wire Thu, October 22, 2026 at 6:00 PM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Arizona Cardinals do not expect to have rookie running back Jeremiyah Love back in Week 7. According to Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports , Love is expected to miss the Cardinals' game against the Denver Broncos on Sunday. Love has been dealing with a lingering ankle injury for weeks. It is not the same ankle he sprained in the preseason. That ankle has healed, and he is not impacted by that. He has played in five games this season. He has rushed for 245 yards and a touchdown, averaging 3.7 yards per attempt. With no Love expected on Sunday, Tyler Allgeier will start and Bam Knight will play in Love's place. Knight rushed for 80 yards against the Rams in Week 6. Evan Hull will likely get elevated from the practice squad. Cardinals' Injury Report is Downright Ugly Skip to main content SI.COM ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals revealed their Thursday injury report for Week 7's clash against the Denver Broncos — and it's not pretty. Darius Robinson and Jon Gaines were added to an already lengthy list of Cardinals that featured Walter Nolen, Budda Baker and Jeremiyah Love among others. Cardinals Thursday Injury Report FULL : Isaac Seumalo (rest), Josh Sweat (rest), Jedrick Wills (illness), The Cardinals, hoping to again play the role of spoiler against Denver, could be massively shorthanded in making that happen as numerous stars are staring down a legitimate possibility of missing time. Baker, Love, Wingard and Nolen have all missed consecutive days of practice now for Arizona. With the Cardinals hoping to take advantage of a disfunctional Broncos offense, Arizona's defense needs all hands on deck. “Last few years. They’re very smart. They’re very well coached," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said of the Broncos' defense. "I have as much respect for ‘VJ’ (Broncos Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph) as anyone in this league. They do it their own way. I don’t want to say they’re not with the times — whatever that means but it’s got an old-school approach to it in terms of some of their coverage and that’s a credit to them. You can tell ‘VJ’ and those guys believe in what they believe in and they’re unapologetic with it. "They play really hard. I see 11 guys working in unison. It’s a challenge. Yes, it’s the last two weeks, but it’s really been all year, and it’s been for a few years now. We have our hands full with this group, for sure.” Published Oct 23, 2026 DONNIE DRUIN Donnie Druin is the Publisher for Arizona Cardinals and Phoenix Suns On SI. The one drawback? He's battled injuries since entering the league. Nolen suffered a calf injury before training camp of his rookie season, which saw him miss the beginning of 2025 before returning halfway through the year. He played a handful of games and showed massive promise before suffering a knee injury that landed him on injured reserve, ending his year. Nolen had surgery (later revealed to be a meniscus) but made a full recovery and was healthy for 2026's training camp, though he suffered a minor lower body injury during the team's time at State Farm Stadium. Last week was the first regular season game Nolen missed for this year. Nolen holds potential to be one of the best young defensive linemen in the NFL, and Arizona certainly needs it. Their defensive line pressure rate of 24.7% ranks dead-last in the league. In a front seven that's been largely uninspiring, Nolen's presence has been noticeable on a weekly basis. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 8 picks, including the Bills to top the Ravens in a high-scoring game Imagn Images Going to the dogs last week turned out to be dog doodoo. I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going. Pick: Packers 31, Panthers 24 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. Pick: Seahawks 24, Bears 17 Now Playing Share Share Video Prisco's Week 8 picks: Packers over Panthers, Lions beat Vikings Bills win Super Bowl? Cowboys take NFC East? picks.blurb: Eleventh hour NFL bold predictions for the Vikings, Broncos and Lions in Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers win World Series Milwaukee can finally celebrate Dybantsa delivers in NBA debut WNBA Finals fatigue Jokić's 200th triple-double Eleventh hour NFL bold predictions for the Vikings, Broncos and Lions in Week 7 Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Oliver Fox Sun, October 25, 2026 at 3:22 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Everything in life always comes in a six-pack or a four-pack -beers, yogurt, sticks of butter, value packs of Pokemon cards . Why do we allow the numbers six and four to dominate our lives like this? On this NFL Sunday morning, I'm here to resist with a three-pack of bold predictions as we careen violently toward kickoff. The streets are saying I just didn't have time to make a six-pack, to which I will tell the streets to shut up because they're literally just made of concrete while I am a luminous being, not this crude matter. The NFC North will feature heavily, and I have more words for Bo Nix; should be a three-packtacular time! The Vikings will blow it against the Colts to lose undefeated streak Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray and wide receiver Justin Jefferson | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect But hey, this is bold predictions, not "pick a touchdown favorite to win" predictions, and the ultimate zag here would be to say that the Colts, who have launched an exploratory committee on trading their entire team , shock everyone by inverting the vibes completely. There isn't a great argument for this to happen, otherwise it wouldn't be bold, but there is an argument. The Vikings offense really is terrible; they are 27th in EPA per play ahead of absolute titans like the ... Tennessee Titans, the Miami Dolphins and the Los Angeles Chargers. They have had real difficulty moving the ball with Kyler Murray under center, and have gimmicked their way to wins with timely turnovers and crazy performance from an aggressive defense. I'm not saying that doesn't work (it clearly works), but there's no way it can work this consistently. The Colts need to stabilize behind their strengths: running the football and managing an efficient offensive attack. In Week 6 against the Titans, it felt like they held some emergency war council meeting at halftime where they all pitched their best ideas on how to best lose the game. If the team can just play to its own strengths rather than allow their weaknesses to consume them, they should have a chance. Bo Nix will be benched in the third quarter against Arizona Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect This is what we call putting the "bold" and "prediction" in bold prediction, because I could have just said something like "Bo Nix will play garbage football again and we'll all hop on our podcasts and blogs and wonder what he does," but let's get real cynical. What if the Broncos and Sean Payton lose their patience completely? Bo Nix is not a good quarterback. I don't know if he's bad, but by every metric imaginable and by the evidence of my own two eyeballs he's been remarkably ineffective this year. He can't really throw over the middle and he can't really throw deep down the sideline, so he basically just runs a college offense with a ton of handoffs, screen passes and dumpoffs with a hysterically low average depth of target. I don't think Jarrett Stidham is any better, nor am I one of those clowns constantly canvassing for unproven backups to start with no evidence that they'll be good. What I know is that the Broncos coaching staff agrees with my assessment of Bo Nix -they trust him with nothing, refuse to call any downfield shots and just try to protect, protect, protect for as long as they can while they win the game with runs, field goals and defense. If they somehow fall down big to Arizona, though? Maybe we see some emergency quarterback switch, if for no other reason than to save face with the rest of the team. Lions defense shows improvement off the bye, limits Green Bay in a big win at home Detroit Lions safety Brian Branch | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Lions defense, so far this year, has been USDA-certified garbage. They have yet to hold a team under 20 points, get cleaved by every elite pass-catcher they encounter and had one of the most unprofessional performances I ever did see on Thursday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills in Week 2. But I, in my infinite wisdom, have decided (for some reason) that this all will get better, and it will get better right now. This is for three reasons: First, the Lions are getting Brian Branch back for the first time all year, a keystone defensive player and the kind of guy they've been missing all season. Second, they're at home, and home field still really matters in football for defensive performance -the only sport where it still really means anything. Third and finally is simple mathematical regression. No defense is in reality this unprofessional, and it's likely if not guaranteed that some of the early-season miscommunications that made the Lions defense so terrible have been ironed out. That's probably factored into the betting line, which is fascinating: Detroit is favored by 3.5 points. They're at home, and their offense is as good as it gets, but Vegas does not buy the Packers recent hot streak at all. Give me the Lions. picks.blurb: Week 8 Fantasy Football Start ‘Em, Sit ‘Em Preview: Detroit Lions vs. Minnesota Vikings - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail My Teams My Teams & Leagues See all Fantasy games See all Fantasy games Week 9 College Football Primer Week 9 College Football Rankings Expert Rankings Play Fantasy Basketball Play Perfect 5 Play Fantasy Hockey Play Fantasy Football Play Death Leagues Play College Fantasy Football 29 Days of Fantasy Fantasy Games Fantasy Baseball Pro Pick'em Survival Football College Pick'em Daily Fantasy Men's Bracket Mayhem Women's Bracket Mayhem Download the App Brewers win World Series Milwaukee can finally celebrate Dybantsa delivers in NBA debut WNBA Finals fatigue Jokić's 200th triple-double (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Dakota Allen Thu, October 29, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFC North is set for a massive showdown as the Detroit Lions host the undefeated Minnesota Vikings (6-0) at Ford Field. From a fantasy football standpoint, this divisional clash presents a fascinating dilemma: Detroit boasts one of the league's most explosive scoring offenses , but Brian Flores' Vikings defense has been the stingiest unit in football, holding opponents to league-low numbers on third downs and in the red zone. Here is how you should manage your key Detroit Lions skill players in fantasy lineups this week. Amon-Ra St. Brown (WR) *Verdict: Mandatory Start (WR1) *The Breakdown: Never overthink your elite talent. Amon-Ra St. Brown remains Jared Goff's undisputed safety valve, commanding a massive target share regardless of game script. While Minnesota's defense excels at limiting big plays downfield, they rely heavily on blitzing to disrupt timing. That operates directly into St. Brown's favor. He thrives on quick-slants, intermediate crossers, and screen setups designed to beat the blitz. Expect heavy volume and a high PPR floor with strong touchdown potential in a high-leverage home game. Jahmyr Gibbs (RB) *Verdict: High-End RB1 Start *The Breakdown: Jahmyr Gibbs is a matchup-proof fantasy asset due to his explosive dual-threat ability out of the backfield. Minnesota's aggressive pass rush often forces opposing quarterbacks to dump the ball off quickly—an area where Gibbs excels. Even if rushing lanes inside are tight against a disciplined Minnesota front seven, Gibbs' involvement in the short passing game gives him a massive ceiling in PPR formats. Lock him into your starting running back slot. Jared Goff (QB) *Verdict: Sit in 1QB Leagues / Low-End Superflex Option * The Breakdown: Goff has been remarkable this season, operating with zero interceptions and elite efficiency. However, Minnesota's defense presents his absolute worst fantasy matchup to date. Brian Flores leads a pass rush tied for the league lead in sacks, generating persistent pressure without sacrificing coverage behind it. Historically, Goff's fantasy output takes a hit when forced off his spot and out of rhythm. Detroit will likely lean on the ground game and methodical short passes, capping Goff's passing yardage and touchdown upside. Look for a safer QB1 alternative if available. Jameson Williams (WR) *Verdict: Risky Flex / Bench Option *The Breakdown: Jameson Williams is the ultimate home-run hitter, but this is a dangerous week to rely on deep shots. Minnesota's primary defensive objective is keeping plays in front of them and preventing explosive vertical completions. Combined with expected edge pressure that limits the time needed for deep routes to develop, Williams carries a dangerously low floor this week. Unless you are chasing high variance in a matchup where you are a heavy underdog, keep "Jamo" on the bench. Sam LaPorta (TE) *Verdict: TE1 Start (Based on position scarcity) *The Breakdown: Tight end remains a thin position across fantasy football, keeping Sam LaPorta in line for starting lineups. However, temper your expectations for a blow-up game. Minnesota has limited tight end production over their six-game winning streak. LaPorta should see targets as a blitz-beater alongside St. Brown, making him a fine start, but expect more of a steady PPR floor than a slate-winning performance.

Mandatory Credit: Brad Rempel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Erik Schlitt Thu, October 29, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Detroit Lions (4-2) and Minnesota Vikings (6-0) will square off in Detroit's second consecutive NFC North battle of the season. "Minnesota is playing outstanding football," Lions coach Dan Campbell said at his Wednesday press conference. (Head coach) Kevin (O'Connell)'s doing a hell of a job. (Defensive coordinator) Brian (Flores) is doing a hell of a job. This thing, they play very complementary football. picks.headline: Vikings at Lions: Predictions, picks and odds for NFL Week 8 game
picks.blurb: 1. Defense wins championships, but will it win this game? The Lions and Vikings couldn't be more opposite at this point in the season. Minnesota is winning with defense, and Detroit is getting by with an electric offense. So it'll be strength vs. strength and weakness vs. weakness in this key NFC North clash. 2. Not-so smooth sailing: The Vikings are about to enter some rough waters when the calendar flips to November. Minnesota cleaned up with wins over the Saints , Dolphins and Colts in October, but the schedule's difficulty is about to be turned up a notch. The Lions, Bills, Packers and Niners await in the penultimate month of the year for the last undefeated team. We're about to find out if the Vikings are a contender or pretender. 3. Scoring drought: For the first time this season, Jahmyr Gibbs didn't get into the end zone. For someone who has his eyes on LaDainian Tomlinson's record of 31, that drought can't last much longer. Gibbs has nine total touchdowns through six games, but he'll still have to pick up the pace. That watch continues into Week 8. Lions vs Vikings odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Lions -4.5 Moneyline: Lions -218; Vikings +180 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Lions vs Vikings USA TODAY expert picks Adam Kaufman: Lions 23, Vikings 20 The Vikings keep winning, and their defense keeps making everybody miserable. That travels. But the Lions present a much tougher offensive assignment than the Colts, especially with Jahmyr Gibbs creating problems as both a runner and receiver. Detroit's best approach is keeping Jared Goff out of obvious passing situations, where Brian Flores can turn an ordinary Sunday into an escape room. Minnesota's historically bad offense remains the concern. Can it consistently hold up its end against a team capable of sustaining drives? I'm expecting a tight, physical division game, with the Lions bouncing back to produce just enough offense to hand the Vikings their first loss. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Lions 20, Vikings 13 This might be the end of the line for the Vikings' undefeated run. While Brian Flores' vise-grip defense gives Minnesota a chance in any contest, it will be exceedingly difficult if the Kyler Murray-led offense remains out of sync. Deroit's defense isn't inspiring fear in anyone, but Brian Branch's return has helped the unit at least approach reliability. Jared Goff has the third-highest passer rating of any quarterback against the blitz this year, so Flores might have to be particularly creative in how he tries to box in the Lions' attack. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Lions 21, Vikings 17 Unstoppable force meets immovable object. The Lions defense couldn't catch a cold this season, and the Vikings offense appears to be doing their best to boost Brian Flores' chances of landing a head coaching job this offseason. If you like chaos, this Flores defense is for you. Physical and blitz-heavy, Minnesota is the last unbeaten team solely because of that unit. However, it's hard to have any faith in the Kyler Murray-led unit on the other side of the ball. This figures to be an ugly NFC North contest. Trust the Lions' offense to eke out a win at home. away.headline: Vikings get positive injury update on RB Aaron Jones: report
away.blurb: The veteran ball carrier exited the game in the fourth quarter as the Vikings posted 10 unanswered points to secure a 16-10 win over the visiting Colts. He was listed as questionable to return, but did not. Minnesota Vikings running back Aaron Jones left Sunday’s win over the Indianapolis Colts with a knee injury. Fortunately for the Vikings, this injury for Jones doesn’t appear to be serious. On Monday, ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter reported a positive update on the Vikings RB. “Vikings RB Aaron Jones’ knee injury that he suffered during Sunday’s win over the Colts is not considered to be significant at this time, and a source described him as ‘day to day,'” Schefter reported. This injury for Jones occurred in the same game that fellow running back Jordan Mason returned from injured reserve. Mason missed each of the Vikings’ last four games after suffering a thumb injury in Week 1, forcing Jones to step up as the team’s bell-cow lead back. Mason led the Vikings in rushing on Sunday, taking 15 carries for 68 yards. Jones recording 26 yards on eight carries before exiting the game. The Vikings are the NFL’s last remaining undefeated team, boasting a 6-0 recording heading into this coming Sunday’s Week 8 matchup against the Detroit Lions. away.headline: Detroit Lions HC Dan Campbell says Kerby Joseph will begin ramp-up process ahead of Vikings matchup
away.blurb: Kerby Joseph begins return-to-play ramp-up: The Lions safety will begin running and gradually reintroducing football activities Wednesday after a lengthy rehabilitation process. No return date announced: Joseph will gradually progress toward explosive movements and drills involving other players. Campbell said more steps remain before he is ready for game action. Lions managing player workloads: Campbell said the team would hold several players, including Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs, out of the practice portion while they participate in the walkthrough. The official injury report should confirm their status for the Vikings game. ALLEN PARK, Mich. — Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell said safety Kerby Joseph will begin the next phase of his return to football activities as the team prepares to host the Minnesota Vikings, offering a positive update on the injured defensive back while emphasizing that more steps remain before he is ready to play. Campbell said the Lions would begin Joseph’s ramp-up process Wednesday, letting him run and gradually return to football activities after a lengthy rehabilitation. “He’s put in a lot of work,” Campbell said. “This has been a long, hard road for Kirby, so just to be able to get back out there with the guys and run around a little bit.” Joseph’s return to the practice environment would also provide an emotional boost for a Detroit team preparing for one of its most significant divisional tests. He did not announce a timetable for Joseph’s return to game action, making clear that the next phase is about determining how the knee responds to the intensity and movement of actual football activities. Campbell also indicated that Detroit would hold several players out of the practice portion of the day’s schedule as the team manages its workload, including Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs . Some players would participate in the walkthrough before sitting out the subsequent practice period. He singled out Minnesota’s defense as the starting point, describing a veteran group that plays with speed, versatility and a strong understanding of Flores’ system. He noted that tight end T.J. Hockenson has seen increased production as Murray has developed a connection with him, while wide receiver Jordan Addison remains a dangerous option despite what Campbell described as limited recent opportunities. Campbell also addressed Detroit’s fourth-down approach, saying his philosophy depends on the matchup, the players available, and his confidence in the play being called. For Detroit, Joseph’s gradual return to football activities is an encouraging development as the team prepares to face Minnesota. away.blurb: Though safety Kerby Joseph made his long-awaited practice return on Wednesday, a number of other Lions stars didn't practice for a variety of reasons. Lions head coach Dan Campbell had said earlier in the day that Detroit was planning to hold some players out. "St.'s doing good, Ennis (Rakestraw Jr.) is doing good. Going to hold them out of practice. We're going to do a walkthrough, and then roll right into practice for a little bit here. So, just kinda, it goes all-in-one. I think those guys will be at walkthrough, but I don't see them out there during the practice portion. I'm going to hold a couple of other guys back just to get them off their feet, but they'll be at walkthrough," Campbell said. But, star running back Jahmyr Gibbs also didn't practice and was listed with a shoulder injury. Fellow running back Jacob Saylors (neck) was a limited participant. Like Campbell said, Amon-Ra St. Brown sat out with his ankle injury, and Rakestraw was a limited participant. Starting defensive lineman Tyleik Williams also didn't practice due to illness. Starting right tackle Brian O'Neill was a limited participant with a knee injury. As Campbell suggested, Aidan Hutchinson, DJ Wonnum, Alim McNeill, and Penei Sewell didn't practice as a scheduled rest day. home.headline: Detroit Lions HC Dan Campbell says Kerby Joseph will begin ramp-up process ahead of Vikings matchup
home.blurb: Kerby Joseph begins return-to-play ramp-up: The Lions safety will begin running and gradually reintroducing football activities Wednesday after a lengthy rehabilitation process. No return date announced: Joseph will gradually progress toward explosive movements and drills involving other players. Campbell said more steps remain before he is ready for game action. Lions managing player workloads: Campbell said the team would hold several players, including Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs, out of the practice portion while they participate in the walkthrough. The official injury report should confirm their status for the Vikings game. ALLEN PARK, Mich. — Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell said safety Kerby Joseph will begin the next phase of his return to football activities as the team prepares to host the Minnesota Vikings, offering a positive update on the injured defensive back while emphasizing that more steps remain before he is ready to play. Campbell said the Lions would begin Joseph’s ramp-up process Wednesday, letting him run and gradually return to football activities after a lengthy rehabilitation. “He’s put in a lot of work,” Campbell said. “This has been a long, hard road for Kirby, so just to be able to get back out there with the guys and run around a little bit.” Joseph’s return to the practice environment would also provide an emotional boost for a Detroit team preparing for one of its most significant divisional tests. He did not announce a timetable for Joseph’s return to game action, making clear that the next phase is about determining how the knee responds to the intensity and movement of actual football activities. Campbell also indicated that Detroit would hold several players out of the practice portion of the day’s schedule as the team manages its workload, including Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs . Some players would participate in the walkthrough before sitting out the subsequent practice period. He singled out Minnesota’s defense as the starting point, describing a veteran group that plays with speed, versatility and a strong understanding of Flores’ system. He noted that tight end T.J. Hockenson has seen increased production as Murray has developed a connection with him, while wide receiver Jordan Addison remains a dangerous option despite what Campbell described as limited recent opportunities. Campbell also addressed Detroit’s fourth-down approach, saying his philosophy depends on the matchup, the players available, and his confidence in the play being called. For Detroit, Joseph’s gradual return to football activities is an encouraging development as the team prepares to face Minnesota. home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Lions, Kerby Joseph had his 3-week window to return from the PUP list opened this week, but he is unlikely to play on Sunday. Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown did not practice Wednesday with shoulder and ankle injuries, respectively, which is something to keep an eye on the rest of the week. For the Vikings, Kevin O'Connell didn't seem overly concerned about either Aaron Jones or Joe Huber. Jones is considered day-to-day while Huber sitting out practice on Wednesday was more precautionary than a sign he won't play on Sunday. Brian O'Neill continues to play through a minor knee injury. We'll see how it plays out with injury updates tomorrow and Friday. picks.blurb: 1. Klint Kubiak vowed there was "no controversy" at quarterback, where Kirk Cousins will remain the starter. While the 38-year-old might have hit a wall last week in trying to navigate the Rams ' relentless blitzes, the NFL's leading passer is hardly the Silver and Black's biggest problem. Kubiak has bemoaned an inert running game that has left Las Vegas needing to sling its way back into games. It could be tricky to get things going against a Jets defense that ranks fifth in defensive EPA per rush. 2. Can New York finally get Garrett Wilson involved early and often in the offensive game plan? One week after he was essentially a non-factor against the Patriots, Wilson was held without a reception or target in the first half against a woefully undermanned Dolphins secondary. Wilson and Glenn both downplayed the wideout's heated confrontation with quarterback Geno Smith, but expect feeding the receiver early and often to be a point of emphasis for Gang Green. 3. How the Raiders' defense handles the Jets' ground game could determine the course of the game. The Silver and Black allowed a season-high 199 rushing yards to the Rams last week, with a vulnerability that has been apparent all season finally reaching critical mass. New York, meanwhile, has seen Braelon Allen eclipse 100 rushing yards in two of the last three games he's handled as Breece Hall's fill-in. Geno Smith gets his former team, while Kirk Cousins keeps the Raiders' starting job despite the growing curiosity about Fernando Mendoza. Neither team has earned much trust lately, so let's acknowledge that before pretending this is an easy handicap. Smith threw three touchdowns against Miami, and Las Vegas' defense offers an opportunity for another productive afternoon. The Raiders need more from their running game to keep Cousins from carrying every possession. I'm giving New York the slightest edge at the Meadowlands, and a fifth straight loss for Las Vegas. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Jets 24, Raiders 20 This game could end up shaping the second half of the season for two coaching staffs that seem to be at a crossroads. The Jets' secondary might not be able to mug the Raiders' receiving corps the way that the Patriots and Rams did, but the pass rush should be able to generate sufficient heat to keep Kirk Cousins out of sorts. Las Vegas seems desperate to find any semblance of offensive balance - as well as some stops against the run - but a breakthrough might not materialize this week. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Raiders 26, Jets 20 You can put a bow on the 2026 Jets. The season, and maybe the Aaron Glenn era, came to an end with a loss to the Dolphins in Week 7. It's going to be a bumpy ride to the finish, but there is no doubt the destination is a top pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. That's why it's fitting that New York will get a glimpse at what it could've had last season. Fernando Mendoza won't play, but it's the idea he's wearing silver and black that sticks. The Raiders are just better. Vegas gets back on track. home.headline: New York Jets Add David Bailey, Braelon Allen to Injury Report
home.blurb: The latest addition is star rookie edge rusher David Bailey, who has a groin injury that is keeping him out of practice on Wednesday. Bailey sustained the injury against the Dolphins, but finished the game. Head coach Aaron Glenn said Bailey came to the Jets practice facility on Monday and said his groin injury was still bothering him. Glenn declined to speculate on whether the injury would keep Bailey out of the game against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. "We'll see how he operates," the coach said. "We'll see during the week." Bailey did not practice on Wednesday, with Glenn waiting until later in the week to make an official game status designation. Of greater concern may be the absence of defensive tackle T'Vondre Sweat. The biggest player in the NFL, Sweat sustained a knee injury against the Dolphins and is listed as doubtful. Also doubtful for the Raiders game is edge Joseph Ossai, who has an ankle injury. Both are considered week-to-week on availability. Also nursing an ankle is running back Braelon Allen, who ran for more than 100 yards against the Dolphins. He was listed as limited for Wednesday's practice. The Jets' other star running back, Breece Hall, may return against the Raiders after being a game-time no-go against the Dolphins. He has 357 yards since Hall went down in Week 3, and has performed so well that the Jets are trying to scheme a way to have both backs on the field at the same time.
