Allen ran for 104 yards on 17 carries against the Dolphins and set a career high with six receptions. "I think you know that Braelon, we also gave him the ball when Breece was with us and playing," Glenn said. "So, I've said this here numerous times: Both of those guys can carry the load. home.blurb: Douglas suffered the ankle ailment in the Sept. 20 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. He returned to practice this week and has been limited in drills Wednesday and Thursday before Friday’s session. After linebacker Willie Gay Jr. popped up on the Thursday injury report due to illness, Hafley said he’s back in the building Friday and feeling better. Gay participated in practice and is deemed questionable to play. The Dolphins have defensive end Rob Beal Jr., who has been back at practice through his hamstring injury, doubtful. Cornerback Reese Taylor, who has hurt quadriceps, is out. Taylor, at least, was seen participating in team stretch and then running and cutting on the side of practice, but he was still deemed a non-participant in practice. Rookie safety Kyle Louis, as he returned to practice this week, appears to be a Saturday decision on whether he is activated off injured reserve with the knee issue suffered in the opener against the Raiders. Listed as questionable, he is at least in play to return. For the Jets, coach Aaron Glenn told reporters Friday running back Breece Hall will be questionable, which held true at the release of the injury report. Hafley said he expects Hall to play after the standout rusher missed three games and he's preparing as such. New York has linebacker and Miami Hurricanes alum Kiko Mauigoa (quadriceps), offensive lineman Max Mitchell (concussion), edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle) ruled out. Questionable, along with Hall, are running back Kene Nwangwu (knee) and offensive lineman Dylan Parham (knee). On Friday, Douglas appeared to be moving well running routes on air and catching passes from quarterback Malik Willis . “He's made a bunch of plays in practice,” said Hafley, who noted Douglas had taken part in individual and team portions of practice before Friday. “I'm excited to see him play. Hafley also said running back Jaylen Wright, who has been dealing with a nagging foot injury, will play. Courtesy of Wednesday's practice report , defensive back Doneiko Slaughter was listed as a non-participant with a hamstring injury. Slaughter was not listed on the Week 7 practice report, and it is not known when he picked up this new hamstring injury. Slaughter, who played collegiate football at Tennessee (2020–2023) and Arkansas (2024), began his NFL career as an undrafted free agent with the Jacksonville Jaguars . Slaughter would later sign a reserve/future contract with the Steelers in January 2026. He was unfortunately released during final roster cuts but subsequently signed with the Steelers' practice squad. Slaughter was elevated from the practice squad for the Steelers' first three games of the season and was signed to the active roster on October 1. He was later waived but ultimately brought back on October 10, where he now remains a vital depth contributor on the 53-man roster. This is the second meeting between the division rivals, with Pittsburgh looking to avenge a loss from the first meeting. The first meeting went down to the wire in Cleveland, and things are different for both teams ahead of the second matchup. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Steelers open up as 3.5 point favorites at home. Vegas believes the game will be a defensive struggle, with the over/under set at 39.5. The Steelers moneyline is set at -198. The Browns have won two straight over Pittsburgh, but both matchups were in Cleveland. Each game was won by one possession. The last regular-season win in Pittsburgh for the Browns happened in 2003. However, the biggest win came in 2020 in the AFC Wild Card round, with Baker Mayfield and the Browns prevailing 48-37. In fact, the 2003 victory is the only regular-season win for Cleveland at Acrisure Stadium. The Steelers have won 12 straight at home against Cleveland, but have dropped five straight in Cleveland. The rivalry is still in Pittsburgh's favor with an 83-66-1 record over the Browns. The Steelers' run defense will have to remain stingy as Quinshon Judkins returned from injury last week and went over 100 rushing yards against Tennessee. The run defense is the seventh-best in the NFL, allowing 91 rushing yards per game and four rushing touchdowns on the season. Meanwhile, the Browns run defense is vulnerable with 116.4 rushing yards allowed per game and four touchdowns allowed. Sticking with the hot hand of Jaylen Warren should be the game plan for Pittsburgh. Rico Dowdle has been involved, and it's clear Mike McCarthy wants to get back to a rotation at running back. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton No one predicted the Browns (5-2) would be tied for first in the AFC North heading into Week 8 of the NFL season, but here they sit as they prepare to play the Steelers (5-2) in Pittsburgh this Sunday. Cleveland has won five of its last six after beating Tennessee 27-24 last Sunday, while Pittsburgh enters on a three-game winning streak following a 16-10 victory over New Orleans in the NFL’s first regular-season game in Paris. The matchup also comes only a month after Cleveland beat Pittsburgh 27-24 on October 1. Last week, Cleveland again showed an ability to win late in their game against Tennessee. After falling behind 14-0 in the first quarter, the Browns rallied behind Quinshon Judkins , who rushed for 96 yards and two touchdowns, and rookie KC Concepcion , who caught eight passes for 129 yards. Deshaun Watson delivered perhaps his best performance of the season, completing 25 of 36 passes for 308 yards while adding a nine-yard rushing touchdown. After Tennessee tied the game with 58 seconds remaining, Watson immediately answered, hitting Harold Fannin Jr. for 36 yards to help set up Andre Szmyt’s game-winning 32-yard field goal as time expired. It was Watson’s fifth fourth-quarter winning drive of the season. Pittsburgh’s latest win was less dramatic but built around the combination it hopes can carry them to a division title and a playoff berth: Aaron Rodgers , an effective running game and a defense capable of closing out tight games. Rodgers completed 19 of 30 passes for 212 yards and a touchdown against New Orleans, including a four-yard score to Darnell Washington that gave him 540 career touchdown passes and moved him past Peyton Manning into third place in NFL history. Jaylen Warren supplied 101 rushing yards on 18 carries. The Pittsburgh defense held the Saints to just 18 rushing yards and Payton Wilson produced a red-zone interception. The biggest storyline may simply be whether Pittsburgh can reverse what happened in Cleveland four weeks earlier. In that Oct. 1 meeting, the Browns built a 21-7 advantage before Rodgers led a fourth-quarter comeback, eventually tying the game at 24 on his three-yard touchdown pass to Pat Freiermuth and ensuing two-point run. Watson then went 4-for-5 for 46 yards on Cleveland’s final drive, positioning Szmyt for a 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds remaining to give the Browns a 27-24 victory. Watson finished with 268 passing yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Rodgers threw for 299 yards and three touchdowns but was intercepted twice; DK Metcalf added 115 receiving yards and Warren ran for 93. That first meeting established the template for Sunday: division rivals comfortable playing close games led by veteran quarterbacks who have repeatedly delivered late, and a Browns team trying to complete an improbable season sweep against a Steelers club returning home looking to reclaim the upper hand in the AFC North. Let’s dive into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. Here’s why the Total UNDER 39.5 is the best bet: The situational and statistical case says this game should land well below 39. Both offenses are genuinely broken in the red zone. Cleveland ranks 27th in touchdown percentage (3.1%), 28th in points scored (19.0 per game), 30th in third-down conversion rate (32.58%), and 32nd in sack rate allowed (11.85%) with 25 sacks taken, most in the NFL. The Browns have run just 10.1% of their offensive plays in the red zone this season — worst in the NFL — and they’re averaging 8.0 drives per touchdown in the second half since 2025, worst in the league. Pittsburgh’s defense is the perfect foil. The Steelers rank 3rd in touchdown percentage allowed (2.59%), 5th in points allowed (19.71 per game), 3rd in touchdowns allowed (11), 5th in passing touchdowns allowed (1.0 per game), 7th in rushing touchdowns allowed (0.57 per game), and 6th in yards per carry allowed (3.75). They’ve allowed opponents to run just 9.5% of plays in the red zone this season — 2nd-best in the NFL. The situational splits are equally ugly for the Over. The Browns have averaged -0.09 EPA per play in the second half since Week 4 — 5th-worst in the NFL — while the Steelers have allowed just -0.17 EPA per play in the second half since Week 4, 2nd-best. Pittsburgh’s defense has allowed -0.18 EPA per play in the second half this season, 2nd-best in the league. Top Player Prop: Browns vs. Steelers Jaylen Warren Anytime Touchdown The best prop on the board, and the volume case is the reason. Warren carried 18 times for 101 yards (5.6 yards per carry) in Pittsburgh’s Week 7 win over New Orleans, and he’s the clear lead back in an offense that has run the ball on just 28% of its red-zone plays — the lowest rate in the league, which means when they do hand it off near the goal line, it’s him. The structural argument is what makes this playable. Pittsburgh ranks 32nd in rushing touchdowns (0.14 per game) — they’ve scored exactly one rushing touchdown all season — which means regression is coming, and Warren is the back who gets those carries. Against a Cleveland defense that ranks 5th in rushing touchdowns allowed (0.57 per game), the volume is the bet rather than the history. away.blurb: The Pittsburgh Steelers were without one of their most underrated depth contributors at Wednesday's practice ahead of their Week 8 matchup against the Cleveland Browns . Courtesy of Wednesday's practice report , defensive back Doneiko Slaughter was listed as a non-participant with a hamstring injury. Slaughter was not listed on the Week 7 practice report, and it is not known when he picked up this new hamstring injury. Slaughter, who played collegiate football at Tennessee (2020–2023) and Arkansas (2024), began his NFL career as an undrafted free agent with the Jacksonville Jaguars . Slaughter would later sign a reserve/future contract with the Steelers in January 2026. He was unfortunately released during final roster cuts but subsequently signed with the Steelers' practice squad. Slaughter was elevated from the practice squad for the Steelers' first three games of the season and was signed to the active roster on October 1. He was later waived but ultimately brought back on October 10, where he now remains a vital depth contributor on the 53-man roster. home.headline: Steelers cornerback misses practice with lingering hamstring injury
home.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
home.blurb: The Pittsburgh Steelers were once again without one of their versatile cornerbacks at practice, as a six-year veteran was held out with a lingering hamstring injury . We at Steelers Wire will monitor Echols' injury situation closely ahead of Week 8, with hopes that he can at least upgrade to limited participation before Sunday's game. Courtesy of Wednesday's injury report, Steelers cornerback Brandin Echols was a non-participant due to a hamstring injury, a health setback that forced him to miss the Week 7 win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris. Echols suffered his hamstring injury during the second quarter of the Week 6 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Echols, who began his career with the New York Jets, joined the Steelers in 2025 free agency. Echols' outside and slot cornerback versatility paid off in a huge way for the Steelers last season, as he appeared in 16 games, including three starts, and recorded 48 combined tackles, two interceptions, and six passes defended. Through six games in 2026, Echols has played just 20 defensive snaps and 97 snaps on special teams. home.blurb: Recently, Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles was asked about the availability of Egbuka, Luke Goedeke, and Antoine Winfield Jr. for Week 8. However, the head coach revealed that all three players remain questionable . "They're all questionable," Bowles said. "We're going to see on Wednesday and Thursday what they do, and I'll have a better answer for you." Egbuka returned to limited practice on Friday ahead of the Panthers matchup, yet he was unable to receive medical clearance in time to play. The latest update leaves Tampa Bay waiting for further clarity on his recovery as the team prepares for its next divisional test. However, Egbuka's recovery from both the concussion and foot injury will ultimately determine whether he can return against Atlanta. Until the Buccaneers provide another update following his upcoming practices, his availability for Week 8 remains uncertain. picks.headline: Early odds and bold Parker Washington prediction for Colts vs. Jaguars in Week 8
picks.blurb: Early odds and bold Parker Washington prediction for Colts vs. Jaguars in Week 8 Skip to main content News FanSided NFL Sites Even though the Jacksonville Jaguars didn't play in Week 7, they managed to gain ground in the AFC South , as every other team in the division lost. The Jags are back from their break and will have a prime opportunity to keep building their lead when they play the hapless Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. The Colts are 2-5 and currently showing no signs of getting better this season. Heck, they let everyone know that they're punting on the season when they ousted general manager Chris Ballard, who failed to replenish the Indianapolis roster and left it devoid of talent. Following the dismissal of Ballard, Indy has gone on to hold a fire sale, sending All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks in return for a 2027 third-round pick and a fifth in 2028 days before the Jaguars game. While the Nelson trade could incentivize the Jags to make a push for defensive tackle DeForest Buckner , they cannot lose sight of the task at hand, which is beating the dreaded divisional foe. And with this in mind, here are the early odds for Week 8 and a bold Parker Washington prediction. The Colts vs. the Jaguars early odds for Week 8 The game will be held at EverBank Stadium, where the Colts have lost 11 consecutive games. Not surprisingly, the Jaguars are a 7.5-point favorite with a moneyline of -395 , via DraftKings. Bet $395 on them to win $100 if they beat Indianapolis for a total payout of $495. The Colts' moneyline sits at +310. Place a wager of $100 and win $310 if they beat Jacksonville for a total payout of $410. The over/under for the game is set at 49.5 points. ** Keep in mind that odds are refreshed periodically, so they can change at any moment. You may also like: 5 Jaguars who need to step up after the bye Bold Parker Washington prediction for the Jaguars vs. the Colts One of the biggest storylines surrounding the Jaguars in the offseason was that they opted not to make a big splash in free agency because they wanted to take care of their homegrown talent. Thus far, they locked up long snapper Ross Matiscik, defensive end Travon Walker, cornerback Montaric Brown, and tight end Brenton Strange, so you could make the case that general manager James Gladstone achieved the goal. That said, Parker Washington is still waiting on an extension. A sixth-round pick in 2023, Washington showed flashed his first two seasons but was stucked behind Christian Kirk. Jacksonville paved the way for him to start when Kirk was traded to the Houston Texans. Right off the bat, Washington became a key contributor on offense, registering 58 receptions for 807 yards with five touchdowns, all career bests, last year. Washington wasted no time picking up where he left off last year, racking up 26 receptions for 416 yards with four touchdowns. The former Penn State Nittany Lion is on pace to register the first 1,000-yard season of his career and should have no trouble getting the top-market contract he's been looking for . Although the Jags reportedly offered Washington $25 million per year before Week 1 , he rejected the offer. It's possible that he's aiming for an annual average of $30 million. Based on his production, he may be able to get it, and he'll have a prime opportunity when he plays the Colts. Already, Washington posted his first 100-yard game of the season against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 5. He'll get his second one in Week 8 when he registers seven receptions for a monster 140 yards with two touchdowns against Indy. away.headline: Jaguars-Colts Wednesday injury report: It is time to unleash Jalen Huskey
away.blurb: Johnson was the only Jaguar who did not practice Wednesday, which is not a great sign coming off a bye week. Johnson injured his ankle in the Week 6 loss to the Houston Texans in London, and the Jaguars very well may be without their best safety once they kick off against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. Limited in practice for the Jaguars were four players: linebacker Jalani Tavai (hamstring), wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring), long snapper Ross Matiscik (shoulder), and defensive tackle Ruke Orhorhoro. JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- There should be one clear reaction to the Jacksonville Jaguars' first injury report of Week 8: it is time for Jalen Huskey. Huskey, the No. 100 pick in April's NFL Draft, has yet to log a snap on defense and has only been active for one game. But the Jaguars should use this week to push Huskey toward some real playing time considering starting safety Antonio Johnson missed Wednesday's practice with an ankle injury. With second-year safety Caleb Ransaw on injured reserve and not looking close to returning anytime soon, the Jaguars' options at safety while Johnson recovers are starting safety Eric Murray, backup safety Kaevon Merriweather, second-year special teamer Rayuan Lane, or Huskey. The Jaguars leaned toward Merriweather getting playing time over Huskey at previous points, but it is time for the Jaguars to unleash their rookie. Merriweather has played 45 NFL games and has been in the NFL since 2023, so naturally he has more experience than Huskey does just a few months into his NFL career. But the Jaguars need to see what they have in their young safety, especially as injuries continue to hit the safety room. Even if the Jaguars start Merriweather over Huskey, they should deploy their third-round defensive back as their No. 3 safety. Simply put, Jacksonville has a young, athletic and talented safety who has been waiting in the wings, and it is time to see what he has. That is not to say Huskey would be the solution to the Jaguars' issues with explosive passes allowed, but he would give the Jaguars a dynamic at the safety position that Lane and Merriweather likely would not. Johnson not playing on Sunday would be a significant blow for the Jaguars' defense considering the impact he has made this season, both in coverage and as a blitzer against the run and rushing the passer. But the Jaguars drafted Huskey for situations like this, and it is time to let him play. With that said, there was some good news for the Jaguars on the injury front. Cornerback Montaric Brown was a full participant after missing time with a hamstring injury that has sidelined him for all but six snaps in the Jaguars' last three games. Brown was struggling at times before his injury, but a healthy Brown would help change the math in the cornerback room and potentially allow the Jaguars to play Jarrian Jones in the slot more than he has played since Brown started missing practice and game reps due to injury. Colts sign CB Kenneth Harris to 53-man roster from practice squad; place CB Cam Taylor-Britt on injured reserve; sign 2 players to practice squad Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE The Colts made the roster moves on Tuesday. The Indianapolis Colts today signed cornerback Kenneth Harris to the 53-man roster from the practice squad and placed cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt on the Injured Reserve list. The team also signed cornerbacks Shemar Bartholomew and Natrone Brooks to the practice squad. Harris, 6-0, 192 pounds, was elevated in Week 7 at Minnesota and Week 1 vs. Baltimore. He has registered three tackles (one solo) and one pass defensed this season. Harris was signed to the team's practice squad on August 31, 2026. He participated in training camp with the Colts after originally signing with the team as a free agent on August 26, 2026. Harris previously participated in the New England Patriots' 2026 offseason program and training camp. He was originally signed by the Patriots as an undrafted free agent on May 8, 2026. Collegiately, Harris played in 59 career games (29 starts) at Oklahoma State (2023-25) and Arkansas State (2020-22) and compiled 113 tackles (92 solo), 61.5 tackles for loss, 1.0 sack, 28 passes defensed and three interceptions. Taylor-Britt, 5-11, 200 pounds, has played in six games this season and has registered seven tackles (three solo), 1.0 tackle for loss, 1.0 sack, two passes defensed and six special teams stops. He has appeared in 53 career games (40 starts) in his time with the Colts (2026) and Cincinnati Bengals (2022-25) and has compiled 210 tackles (154 solo), 5.0 tackles for loss, 1.5 sacks, 40 passes defensed, seven interceptions (two returned for touchdowns), two forced fumbles and six special teams stops. away.headline: Injured Chargers Safety Derwin James Jr. Has Suffered a Setback, Could Go on IR
away.blurb: Starting left guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), cornerback Deane Leonard (concussion), wide receiver Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) and edge rusher Khalil Mack (veteran rest day) didn't practice. Cornerbacks Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley, both of whom have bad hamstrings, and wide receiver Tre' Harris (hamstring) were limited participants. But there is particular concern about yet another Chargers player who has a hamstring injury and sat out practice on Wednesday. Injured Chargers Safety Derwin James Jr. Has Suffered a Setback, Could Go on IR - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Milwaukee can finally celebrate Jokić's 200th triple-double Injured Chargers Safety Derwin James Jr. Has Suffered a Setback, Could Go on IR Robert Marvi Thu, October 29, 2026 at 4:51 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads What has been a season of horrors for the Los Angeles Chargers isn't getting any easier for them. Coming off their bye week, they held practice on Wednesday in preparation for their contest this Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams, and the news wasn't good. With a 0-6 record, the Chargers have little, if anything, to play for the rest of this season. They're currently dealing with a number of injuries to key players, and on Wednesday, five men didn't take part in practice. Injured reserve is a possibility for a key Chargers defender Safety Derwin James Jr., who has missed each of L.A.'s last three games, reportedly suffered a setback and didn't participate in practice on Wednesday. Head coach Jim Harbaugh said that James could go on injured reserve, per Noah Furtado of The Athletic . James, a five-time Pro Bowler, has seen his game slip so far this season. In three games, he has just one pass defended, and he's allowing a 101.7 passer rating when targeted in pass coverage. Last season, he allowed a 57.8 passer rating when targeted in coverage while posting seven passes defended, three interceptions, two sacks, eight quarterback hits and six tackles for loss. He doesn't have a single sack, QB hit or tackle for loss so far this year. The 30-year-old James is under contract through the 2029 season and will be owed over $24 million apiece in 2028 and 2029. He has been mentioned as a trade candidate, and the Chargers have plenty such players, starting with Mack. In good injury news for Los Angeles, wide receiver Ladd McConkey was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. He had suffered a concussion in the team's last game, which was a 22-6 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on Oct. 18. home.headline: Sean McVay hints Davante Adams could return from injury after Rams' Week 11 bye
home.blurb: Per Charean Williams of Pro Football Talk, Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters on Wednesday that Adams' return will probably be "closer to the shorter term" of the previously mentioned timeline. As of the final Thursday of October, it was far too early for any outsider to guess whether or not Adams could be available for the Thanksgiving Eve matchup versus Green Bay. However, it sounds like there is at least a chance that he could be in the lineup that evening. Shortly after it was learned that star Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Davante Adams suffered a ruptured hamstring in the Rams' Week 6 loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 18, a report revealed he was expected to miss 6-10 weeks of action. It sounds like Adams won't need a full 10 weeks of recovery before he's back in the Rams' lineup. Sean McVay: "Wolverine" Davante Adams could be back sooner rather than later "He tells me, which I believe, [that] he’s Wolverine," McVay said about Adams while referencing the Marvel Universe character. "He’ll heal quick and be ready to go. He’s in good spirits. [He] sent me a picture the other day [of him] being able to walk already. He’s doing really well, and I think, based on how everything went, on the shorter end is what is projected." Adams didn't play in the Rams' 35-21 win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Oct. 25. Nevertheless, ESPN stats show that he ranks third on the Rams with 30 receptions, second with 49 targets, second with 480 receiving yards and first with four touchdown grabs. Davante Adams' hamstring procedure "went really well" Adams recently had successful surgery on his left hamstring. "Everything’s good," McVay said about that procedure. "It went really well. He’s feeling good in the process of recovering and doing really well." Adams is on track to remain sidelined for games against the Los Angeles Chargers, Washington Commanders and Cardinals. The Rams will then enter their bye week before they begin preparing for their Nov. 25 home game against the Green Bay Packers. Want more articles like this? home.headline: Report: Rams WR Puka Nacua's injury not believed to be serious
home.blurb: Oct 23 (Field Level Media) - Rams receiver Puka Nacua sustained a calf injury in practice Thursday that is not expected to be serious, NFL Network reported. Per the report, his status is "up in the air" for the Rams (2-4) for Sunday's road game against the Las Vegas Raiders (3-3). Los Angeles head coach Sean McVay is expected to speak to reporters on Friday. The Rams will be without fellow wideout Davante Adams, who was placed on injured reserve earlier in the week with a ruptured hamstring. The other members of the receiver room are Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Alex Bachman. Nacua, 25, has 37 catches for 417 yards and one touchdown to go with one rushing score in four games this season. He missed two games with a psoas injury. A two-time Pro Bowl selection, Nacua led the NFL with 129 receptions last season and racked up 1,715 receiving yards with 10 touchdowns in 16 games.

home.headline: Trent McDuffie breaks silence on injury, says Rams have rediscovered swagger
home.blurb: McDuffie attempted to return last Friday ahead of the Rams’ Week 7 showdown with the Raiders, but the team’s medical staff decided another week of recovery was the smarter approach. McDuffie was a limited participant Wednesday, but his excitement about returning to the practice field was impossible to hide. “Man, biggest smile on my face while I was out there, back on the football field,” he said. “We won’t win a game unless we figure out how to not beat ourselves,” coach Sean McVay said after the team’s embarrassing 18-16 loss to the Cardinals at home in Week 6. Untimely penalties, undisciplined football, questionable coaching decisions and self-inflicted mistakes transformed a Super Bowl favorite into a last-place team in the NFC West. “Guys had that confidence, guys had that swagger and guys were just going out there enjoying being out there with each other,” McDuffie said. “Take the pressure off. Let the score be the score. Let the record be whatever it is. Let’s just go out there and enjoy these last games that we have with each other.” Trent McDuffie spent Sunday watching from the sidelines as the Rams finally began looking like the Super Bowl contenders everyone expected them to be. Now the All-Pro cornerback wants back in on the action. After missing the last two games with a groin injury suffered in practice two weeks ago, McDuffie returned to the field on Wednesday and told the California Post in an exclusive interview that he’s feeling better and ready to suit up against the Chargers if the medical staff gives him the green light. “If I’m cleared, man, I’m ready to go,” McDuffie said with a smile. Trent McDuffie back at practice for the Rams for the first two time in 2 weeks. pic.twitter.com/dMMhsHyVO3 McDuffie revealed that he felt tightness and a slight tug in his groin, an injury that required patience rather than pushing through the pain and risking a more significant setback. “For me, it was just tightness. I felt a little tug, a little groin strain,” McDuffie said. “It was one of those injuries you’ve got to be careful with. You push it too much, you can kind of make it worse.” “I told them last week, ‘I’m going to give you every single second I’ve got to try to make the game,'” McDuffie said. “They just thought taking an extra week would be smart, so that’s what we did.” The decision appears to have paid off. Before the season began, McDuffie told The Post that the biggest threat to the Rams’ championship aspirations wasn’t the Seahawks, 49ers or anybody else on their schedule. Through the first six weeks of the season, McDuffie’s proclamation proved to be right, as the Rams scuffled to a 2-4 start, finding new creative ways to beat themselves week after week. But Sunday’s 35-21 victory over the Raiders offered a glimpse of what the Rams could become if they stopped stepping on their own feet. “The energy was right. The Los Angeles Rams remain uncertain about Myles Garrett’s return from knee surgery as Sean McVay weighs the next step in the star defensive end’s recovery ahead of their Week 8 clash with the Chargers. Los Angeles Rams have no clear date for Myles Garrett's return McVay has yet to decide whether the Rams will open Garrett's 21-day practice window, which would allow the defensive end to begin working toward a return. Speaking to reporters on October 26, the coach said he needed to consult the team's medical staff before making that call. Early reports suggested he might return after four weeks, but the recovery period later stretched to six weeks or longer. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported last week that Garrett was likely to return to practice, with a possible Week 8 appearance in the discussion. Opening the practice window would not guarantee an immediate return to games. The Rams would have 21 days to activate Garrett to the 53-man roster or place him on season-ending injured reserve. Until the team makes that move, he cannot play. Other reports have suggested the wait could continue. ESPN's Dan Graziano reported on October 21 that Garrett was likely to miss at least another two or three weeks. That timeline could push his return toward Week 10, with the Rams scheduled to have a bye in Week 11. Los Angeles improved to 3-4 after beating the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7, but the team has little room for further setbacks. picks.headline: Week 8 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Chiefs look to bounce back vs. Broncos
picks.blurb: Week 8 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Chiefs look to bounce back vs. Broncos - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers win World Series Milwaukee can finally celebrate Dybantsa delivers in NBA debut WNBA Finals fatigue Jokić's 200th triple-double Frank Schwab Senior writer Thu, October 29, 2026 at 12:41 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the Denver Broncos, Week 1 had to feel like a bad flashback. The first 12 times that Patrick Mahomes started against the Broncos, the Kansas City Chiefs were 12-0. Then there was a shift with Sean Payton in charge, and the Broncos won two of three against Mahomes and the Chiefs. Then the season opener was like old times. It wasn't Mahomes that ruined the Broncos in the opener, though he played pretty well. It was Kenneth Walker III doing most of the damage as he ran through many missed tackles by the Broncos for 173 rushing yards. Also, the Chiefs' defense shut down Denver in a 31-10 win. It was a complete, impressive performance. It doesn't seem like much has changed since then. The Chiefs started 5-0 before losing last week at Seattle, a very tough opponent. The Broncos are 5-2 but questions persist about their offense. Denver's defense has played much better since that weird off night at Kansas City, however. While the defense on the whole has been better for the Broncos, the run defense isn't great. They're 26th in EPA ( expected points added ) per rush allowed. It's easy to say that the Seahawks showed everyone how to beat the Chiefs and that's to take Walker out of the game, but not everyone has Seattle's defense to pull that off. The Broncos showed once they aren't a great matchup against Walker. That's a big reason Kansas City -1.5 is the pick. We saw in the season opener that the Chiefs' dominance over the Broncos might not be over. Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III had 173 rushing yards in Week 1 against the Broncos. (AP Photo/Colin E. Braley) Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 8 of the NFL season: Panthers (+3.5) over Packers There's no way the Panthers are as bad as they played last week, when they were down 33-6 to the Buccaneers by halftime. Competent teams that get embarrassed usually bounce back well. The Packers are still a tough team to predict. Raiders (+1.5) over Jets The early East Coast start has been death for the Raiders for a long time. But they are probably the better team. Certainly the better coached team. The Raiders are on a four-game losing streak but look at the opponents: Chiefs, Patriots, Bills, Rams. Those are four of the strongest teams in the NFL. If Las Vegas can't win here, it might be Fernando Mendoza time. Cowboys (-6.5) over Cardinals The Cowboys are going to score. The Cardinals have given up at least 30 points in six of their eight games. Dallas showed on Monday night that its offense is back. But what about Dallas' defense? Maybe a strong fourth quarter against the Eagles is a sign that the Cowboys' defense can be somewhat competent. It's scary to pick the Cowboys laying points to anyone because they'll need to get stops, but it would be a surprise if they don't score 30. Buccaneers (-2.5) over Falcons Good luck figuring out either of these teams. The Buccaneers could be better than we think. Their only significant weakness has been pass offense, and that is explained by having an undrafted rookie starting three of their seven games. We don't know if Baker Mayfield is fully healthy, considering he had just 11 pass attempts in his return from a dislocated right thumb last week, but if he is maybe the Bucs can get on a roll. Browns (+3.5) over Steelers Teams coming back from an international game and playing right away without a bye are 0-3-1 this season. The losses were by 12, 11, and 6 points, and the close loss was by the Texans as a 10-point favorite last week. The tie was the Commanders when they were favored at home against the Giants. It's a hard turnaround, and it's what the Steelers face coming back from Paris last Sunday. Both of these teams are 5-2 but flawed, and I'll ride with the angle of the Browns not being the team that played in France last week. Jaguars (-9.5) over Colts It's hard to imagine being a Colts player this week. Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner were traded and everyone else with any value has to wonder if they're next. It's actually surprising the line is less than 10 points against a Jaguars team coming off a bye and a loss. This could get really ugly. The remainder of the Colts' season could get really ugly. Ravens (+3.5) over Bills You've seen this here before: This all depends on if Lamar Jackson plays. This week, I assume he will. It seemed like he was close last week and he practiced in full on Wednesday. There would be some real frustration if he's not back for this game, which Baltimore might need to win to start to save its season. Their remaining schedule is the toughest in the NFL according to DVOA . If he does play, we know the Bills defense is not very good. Getting more than a field goal seems good. Vikings (+3.5) over Lions If the Vikings' build was reversed, and they had a fun offense that was clearly one of the two best in the sport but a defense that was unreliable and among the 10 worst in the NFL, we'd respect them more. How do we know that? The 2026 Buffalo Bills, that's how. Minnesota's defense has been remarkable. Look at the Chicago Bears this season. In three of Caleb Williams' four starts, Chicago is averaging 39 points. In the other start, against the Vikings, the Bears scored three points at home (Williams got injured in that game but not until mid-fourth quarter). Maybe Detroit will figure out Brian Flores' defense, but nobody else has and I'm willing to take more than a field goal. Titans (+10.5) over Bengals The Titans have been blown out only twice. They lost by 13 to the Jets in Week 1 and 23 to the Texans in Week 5. Every other game has been decided by six or fewer points. The Titans have won only one of those games, but they're keeping it close. It's possible Joe Burrow will add to his growing MVP argument and torch Tennessee in a blowout, but this seems like a good spot for an ugly underdog. Rams (-6.5) over Chargers Typically, an 0-6 team coming off a bye would be a fine choice. The Chargers don't want to get embarrassed all season. But they're simply not a good team in any phase. That is shocking but also irrefutable. This is the exact type of contrarian pick I'd like to make but I just can't get there with the Chargers. Patriots (-7) over Dolphins It's possible the Dolphins get some confidence from their first win. It's also possible they let down a bit: It's still a 1-5 team whose goal was to get that first win out of the way. On the other side, there's a Patriots team coming off a loss with three extra days of rest. Commanders (-5.5) over Eagles A low point of this week was looking at the schedule and realizing this was the Sunday night game. Not fun. Not sure what's more surprising: That a 1-4-1 Commanders team is a 5.5-point favorite over the Eagles, or that the Commanders are the pick. The Eagles' best remaining effort was going to come on a Monday night against the rival Cowboys, and that effort was pretty meager. It won't get better. Bears (+3) over Seahawks The Sunday night game might not be good, but Monday night makes up for it. This one is fun (and should have been the Week 1 opener, but that's an old gripe). If there's an offensive coach that can figure out the Seahawks' defense, it's Ben Johnson. Caleb Williams has been on a heater since returning from a hamstring injury. On the other side, Seattle's offense will be happy to see the Bears defense after a tough stretch of opposing defenses, and perhaps Jaxon Smith-Njigba goes nuts against a questionable Bears defense. It should be a good game, and if that holds it'll be nice to have the underdog. Last week : 5-8-1 Season to date: 46-58-2

picks.headline: Broncos vs Chiefs preview: Denver attempts a redo
picks.blurb: Broncos vs Chiefs preview: Denver attempts a redo - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers win World Series Milwaukee can finally celebrate Dybantsa delivers in NBA debut WNBA Finals fatigue Jokić's 200th triple-double Broncos vs Chiefs preview: Denver attempts a redo KANSAS CITY, MO - SEPTEMBER 14: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos reacts after a play against the Kansas City Chiefs during the second half of an NFL football game at Arrowhead Stadium on September 14, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ian St. Clair Wed, October 28, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The first game of the 2026 season for your Denver Broncos did not go according to plan. Not that anyone in Broncos Country needs a reminder. Denver was flogged 31-10 by the Kansas City Chiefs. And the Broncos defense still hasn't tackled Kenneth Walker. Thankfully, and hopefully, Denver gets a crack at a redo this Sunday in Denver. A win at home against Patrick Mahomes, Walker, and Kansas City would give the Broncos the lead in the AFC West. FanDuel Sportsbook has Denver as the home underdog at +1.5 points, though that's basically a pick 'em at this point. The total sits over/under 40.5 points, with a lean toward the over at -115. Offensive Rankings Kansas City : Sixth in total offense (380.5 yards per game), fifth in rushing offense (141.5 YPG), 11th in passing offense (239.0 YPG), 14th in scoring offense (23.8 points per game). Denver : Thirtieth in total offense (270.0 yards per game), 24th in rushing offense (94.9 YPG), 27th in passing offense (175.1 YPG), tied for 24th in scoring offense (20.6 points per game). Defensive Rankings Kansas City : Fourteenth in total defense (323.3 yards per game), 13th in rushing defense (99.5 YPG), 17th in passing defense (223.8 YPG), second in scoring defense (17.2 points per game). Denver : Twenty-third in total defense (349.0 yards per game), 28th in rushing defense (133.3 YPG), 12th in passing defense (215.7 YPG), seventh in scoring defense (20.1 points per game). Here are the MHR staff's keys to Sunday's game. Win the turnover battle As we saw in the Thursday night win over the Seattle Seahawks, when the Broncos defense creates turnovers and the offense protects the ball, Denver wins. The Broncos have been better at creating takeaways this season, and they need to carry that over on Sunday. Force Mahomes into some rushed throws and/or punch the ball out to give Bo Nix and the offense some added possessions. On top of that, Nix and the offense need to continue to protect the ball. Win the turnover battle on Sunday, and the Broncos put themselves in a great spot to win the game. — Ian St. Clair Stop the Chiefs run game Mahomes is continuing to play based off who he was two years ago and not putting in the effort to stay great. I like our chances if we force him to throw on our excellent secondary. Stop Kenneth Walker and win the game. — Sadaraine Tackle Kenneth Walker III The Broncos were hanging tough in the first half in that Week 1 matchup, but the horrific tackling eventually led to big plays in the run game. The Chiefs ran away from Denver in the second half. We all remember how much we overreacted to that first game, but man, did they miss too many tackles to count, and the overreaction was warranted. Since then, however, the Broncos defense has been pretty damn good and the offense is finally waking up. Keep up that momentum, and they should take care of business this weekend. — Tim Lynch Feed Jonah Coleman No need to get cute. Let Jonah Coleman build off the game he had against the Arizona Cardinals. Commit to the running attack. Get the young guys involved. Coleman and RJ Harvey had great games in Phoenix. Keep that going. The passing attack will open up once teams are forced to respect the run. — Adam Malnati Score more points than KC Using advanced analytics, the keys to this game are simple. When the Broncos score fewer points than their opponent, they are 0-2, and when they score more, they are 5-0. Further proving this point, they are 0-1 vs. the Chiefs this season when scoring fewer points than them. However, they were 2-0 against the Chiefs last season when they scored more points than their division rivals. So, according to these advanced analytics, if they can score more points than the Chiefs in this game, they will be 6-2. — Scotty Payne What are your keys to Sunday's game?

picks.headline: Chiefs at Broncos: Predictions, picks and odds for NFL Week 8 game
picks.blurb: 1. With Kenneth Walker III coming to town, the Broncos will be called on to clean up an operation that missed 28 tackles in the Chiefs' season-opening romp. Kansas City surely wants to get the Super Bowl 60 MVP back to his early-season form after the Seahawks kept him in check. Denver has shown signs in recent weeks of its run defense coalescing, but Sunday will mark a stiff test after the group overwhelmed shorthanded backfields in the last two weeks. 2. Injuries loom large in the matchup between the Chiefs' aerial attack and the Broncos' vaunted pass defense. Getting receiver Rashee Rice and right tackle Jaylon Moore back could provide a significant boost to a Kansas City attack coming off arguably the worst offensive outing of Patrick Mahomes' tenure. But Denver could also get significant reinforcements with cornerback Patrick Surtain II trying to play after sitting out three weeks with an ankle injury. 3. A methodical Denver offense finally found its explosive streak last week against Arizona, with Bo Nix and RJ Harvey both reeling off long touchdowns. Repeating that effort against the Chiefs could be difficult, especially with Jaylen Waddle's status in question after he suffered a chest injury late against Arizona. But the emergence of rookie running back Jonah Coleman, who had 93 rushing yards in his first game back from injured reserve, could help the Broncos avoid the obvious passing situations that plagued the team early in the season. Broncos vs Chiefs odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Broncos -1 Moneyline: Broncos -125; Chiefs +105 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Broncos vs Chiefs USA TODAY expert picks Adam Kaufman: Chiefs 23, Broncos 20 Three points. That's all Kansas City managed in Seattle on the way to its first loss. I'm expecting a response, although Denver is hardly the place to assume everything gets fixed, especially after seeing multiple come-from-behind wins for the home team this year at Mile High. The Broncos have won three straight, but their injury picture matters, particularly with Patrick Surtain II and Jaylen Waddle. The Chiefs have their own issues to sort through, and the Week 1 blowout doesn't tell us how this rematch will unfold. We should get a considerably tighter game, with both defenses making the offenses work. I'm not sure I trust Patrick Mahomes, given the lack of quality pass-catchers around him, but I do trust Kenneth Walker III against one of the NFL's worst run defenses on the heels of a homecoming dud. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Chiefs 17, Broncos 10 Even with all of their readily evident limitations, it's hard to believe the Chiefs could turn up truly putrid offensive performances in back-to-back weeks. Denver, on the other hand, might be dealing with its own regression to the mean, as it seems unlikely that last week's explosive plays will carry over against the Chiefs. A rout similar to Week 1 might not be in the cards, but Kansas City should be able to escape with the sweep. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Broncos 20, Chiefs 16 This should be a marquee game, but now it feels like just another game on the Sunday slate – due in part to a sleep-inducing Broncos' offense and very flawed Chiefs team. Kansas City's Week 1 blowout victory over Denver feels like a lifetime ago, and maybe that's because it was. Bo Nix showed some signs of life last week, while Patrick Mahomes is running out of receivers. If the Chiefs can't win by handing the ball off to Kenneth Walker III, they can't win. Denver knows that. We know that. The home team wins in the Mile High City. picks.headline: Chiefs-Broncos betting line & game prediction: Can KC solve problems in Denver?
picks.blurb: Read our AI Policy. The Chiefs enter Denver at 5-1 after a 20-3 loss to the Seahawks Sunday night. Denver has won three straight games, including a 30-16 win over Arizona. The betting line lists Kansas City as a 1.5-point favorite against Denver. The Kansas City Chiefs seek to rebound from their first loss of the season Sunday when they travel to take on the Denver Broncos. The Chiefs lost to the Seattle Seahawks 20-3 Sunday night, dropping to 5-1. Meanwhile, the Broncos won their third straight game — a convincing 30-16 victory over the Arizona Cardinals — to improve to 5-2. How to watch Chiefs at Broncos Kickoff: 3:25 p.m. Central Where: Empower Field at Mile High Stadium in Denver TV: CBS (Channel 5 in Kansas City) Radio: KFNZ (96.5 FM in Kansas City, KNSS 98.7 FM in Wichita) Betting line: Chiefs -1.5 Behind the DEN-KC matchup Just seven weeks ago on Monday Night Football, running back Kenneth Walker made his Chiefs debut against the Broncos at Arrowhead Stadium — and it would be fair to say he embarrassed the opposition. Walker gashed Denver for 173 rushing yards and 191 yards from scrimmage, scoring twice in a 31-10 win . The production was one thing; the humiliating aspect was how he did it. The Broncos missed 28 tackles as a team, including 14 broken by Walker. Walker’s explosive opening-night performance established a recipe for success that Kansas City followed over the next four games — all Chiefs victories. That came to a screeching halt last week against the Seahawks. Guided by head coach Mike Macdonald, who knew Walker well, the Seattle defense seemingly swarmed him upon every touch, emphasizing multiple players rallying to the ball. Macdonald’s shrewd defensive plan limited Walker to just 36 rushing yards — and Kansas City to three points. With Walker contained, the Chiefs had to turn to the pass, opening the door for the Seahawks’ talented front to tee off on quarterback Patrick Mahomes . Seattle pressured Mahomes on more than half of his dropbacks, and with receivers Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) and Tyquan Thornton (ankle) sidelined, the Chiefs had no answer. “They did a good job with the pressure package, and we’ve got to do better,” Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said. In a copycat league, Seattle may have provided a blueprint for Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph, one of the best defensive minds in the league. If Denver keys in on Walker, Kansas City has to find another way. “Whenever teams are going to try to stop Kenneth, we have to be able to counteract that,” Mahomes said Wednesday. “And I think that’s something that’ll be big the rest of the season. Obviously, Kenneth is a special player, and he makes a lot of big plays happen, and we’re not going to stop trying to run the football. “But if they’re going to put so many resources into stopping him and playing a shell over the top, we have to be able to hit them in that intermediate area.” Attacking the intermediate areas of the field should be more manageable against the Broncos if Rice and right tackle Jaylon Moore (concussion) return to the lineup. Rice was limited in practice Wednesday , while Moore was a full participant. Moore, left tackle Kahlil Benson and the interior offensive linemen will once again need to manage edge rusher Nik Bonitto and first-team All-Pro defensive lineman Zach Allen (hamstring) — the most disruptive members of Denver’s front. Allen did not practice Wednesday but has told reporters he may “possibly” play against the Chiefs. Three-time All-Pro cornerback Patrick Surtain II was a full participant Wednesday and is eyeing a return to the lineup after a three-game absence. With the Chiefs coming off their worst offensive performance of the season, the Broncos are coming off their best offensive performance since Week 2. Against the Cardinals, quarterback Bo Nix completed 15 of 29 passes for 222 yards and a touchdown, adding a team-leading 73 rushing yards on seven attempts. Denver’s first touchdown came on Nix’s 62-yard run. After studying the film, Chiefs linebacker Nick Bolton sees a significant difference between the Broncos Kansas City faced in Week 1 and the team they are now. “They found some things that worked for them,” Bolton said. “I think Bo is doing a good job using his feet, getting the ball to his ball-catchers, trusting his O-line, sticking with the run game. I think one of the things after our game was they stick with the run. They’ve been doing that a little bit better the last couple of games.” Unlike the Chiefs, the Broncos feature a three-headed running back rotation of JK Dobbins, RJ Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman. In his first game off of injured reserve against Arizona, Coleman led the room with nine carries for 54 yards, adding two catches for 15 yards through the air. When Harvey is on the field, the Chiefs will need to be ready for the checkdown, as he already has 25 catches for 217 receiving yards on the season. The difference for the Broncos against the Cardinals was explosive plays, as they produced five gains of at least 20 yards. Kansas City will also need to fare better on third down than it did against Seattle, which converted 11 of 16 attempts. One injury to monitor for Denver is wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest), who exited Sunday’s game. Waddle did not practice Wednesday. According to SumerSports , Waddle has taken the most snaps in the slot for Denver this season (105), followed by wide receiver Courtland Sutton (75) and tight end Evan Engram (65). Even if Waddle doesn’t play, the Chiefs will need to defend the slot better against the Broncos than they did against the Seahawks. Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba posted nine catches for 150 yards and a touchdown, including 68 yards from the slot. Slot cornerback L’Jarius Sneed (personal/knee), who missed practice Wednesday, had to be replaced inside last game after struggling mightily in the first half. The Chiefs’ struggles against Seattle extended to special teams, with kicker Harrison Butker missing 2 of 3 field goals . The misses stifled what little momentum Kansas City had, contributing to the club’s controversial decision Wednesday to sign veteran Justin Tucker to the practice squad. Reid insisted that Tucker was signed for “security” and said Butker would receive most of the practice reps this week and likely start Sunday in Denver. A month removed from their first meeting, these teams already look different. That could be just fine for the Chiefs, so long as the result remains the same. Broncos-Chiefs game prediction What once had been a regularity for the Chiefs has actually become a scarcity. The last time the Chiefs defeated the Broncos in Denver was January 2022 — in the 2021 regular-season finale. The Broncos’ defense is playing a lot better than it did in Week 1, and Bo Nix has regained some confidence. I still don’t trust him, not against Mahomes. Through their first five games, Walker made the Chiefs feel like wins come easy. Last week’s lopsided loss reminded them they don’t. Kansas City responds in an old-school, grind-it-out divisional game to get back on track. Also ruled out for the Seahawks are linebacker Drake Thomas , who will be out for the second week in a row due to an ankle injury, and linebacker Chazz Surratt , who will be missing a fourth straight game with a calf injury. Also questionable are outside linebackers DeMarcus Lawrence (knee) and Uchenna Nwosu (hip), both of whom were limited for the second straight day, backup quarterback Drew Lock , who has been limited all week with a right elbow injury, and outside linebacker Connor O'Toole (hamstring), who was limited Friday after not practicing the previous two days. Left tackle Josh Simmons, who already missed the first five games of the season with a back injury, was placed on injured reserve earlier this week. home.headline: Broncos' first injury report for Week 8 paints an early bleak picture
home.blurb: Of note, Patrick Surtain II pracitced in full, so the Broncos should get him back, but all of Allen, Waddle, and Talanoa Hufanga did not practice: The initial report with Waddle was that he aggravated his chest injury, but that there is 'hope' he can play on Sunday. Hufanga has already missed a couple of games due to his ankle injury, and if he does not practice in some capacity on Thursday, his status for Week 8 is in doubt. Allen has a hamstring injury and did not practice, either. The weird thing is that there was not any sort of report that came out with Allen's injury like we saw with Waddle, so that could end up being good news that it's pretty minor. We're definitely not going to make any declarations here since it's early in the week, but the Thursday statuses are going to be huge, as if any of the three "DNP" players from Wednesday are limited or full on Thursday, their chances of playing go way up. Sean Payton hilariously called himself out for awful Jaylen Waddle play call The Denver Broncos have consistently been among the healthiest teams in the NFL since Sean Payton took over back in 2023. That doesn't mean, though, the team has not dealt with injuries. Every NFL team has to deal with injuries in some capacity, and the teams that are usually standing in the end have better depth or better roster health overall. In Week 7, a win over the Arizona Cardinals, the Broncos saw two key players leave the game in wide receiver Jaylen Waddle, and defensive end Zach Allen. And in the team's first injury report of Week 8, we see some key players on the report, and while it is early, their statuses for Week 8 could already be in doubt. Denver Broncos injury report is getting longer as Week 8 approaches However, if any of them again do not practice on Thursday, it would logically be unlikely that they play on Sunday. While the Broncos are more talented than Kansas City and get this game at home, not having even one of these players is going to be brutal. In the same way that 2025's home game against the Chiefs was important, this one is as well. The Broncos would be in first place in the AFC West with a win, but if they lose, the Chiefs would improve to 6-1, and Denver would drop to 5-3 with two losses to the Chiefs already etched into their record. It would severely hurt their chances at repeating as division champions. And as it concerns the pasing game, if the Broncos hope to build on their breakout from Week 7, having Waddle in the lineup would allow that to continue to happen. Hufanga remains on the wrong side of questionable after missing the last two games due to an ankle injury. The former AFC Defensive Player of the Week will need to get in at least limited practices on Thursday and Friday to have a shot at suiting up versus Kansas City. Allen's apparently hamstring ailment is a new development, though one that, as of this writing, seems unlikely to hold him out of Week 8 action. Elsewhere on the injury report, left tackle Garett Bolles (hip) and wide receiver Marvin Mims (ankle) were considered limited, while cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle), defensive tackle Malcolm Roach (neck), and inside linebacker Karene Reid (elbow) were full participants. Surtain appears poised to return from a three-game absence as his ankle presumably is at or near full health. Of note on the Chiefs' end, cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (personal/knee) did not practice on Wednesday while receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) was limited, and quarterback Patrick Mahomes (knee) and tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) were full goes. “I think to his credit, whenever we ask something of him—whether it’s intermediate, down the field—he’s been really effective," he said of Mims on Wednesday. "Obviously as a returner, that first return with the ball midfield, those are... I’ve said this before, the receiving now to start the game. [At] minimum there’s a threshold, but to start where we started, those are things that he’s shown us consistently. He continues to have those touches and then where you want to even get him more touches. It’s sometimes a challenge, but certainly he’s deserving.” The Denver Broncos released their initial Week 8 injury report ahead of Sunday's pivotal home showdown against the Kansas City Chiefs. An earlier report indicated that Waddle suffered a re-aggravation of a prior chest issue toward the end of last week's victory over the Arizona Cardinals, and his status for Sunday's game is to be determined. The injury occurred on a trick play that head coach and offensive playcaller Sean Payton consequently apologized for. "Why didn't anybody ask me about the dumb reverse call? ... It was awful. I'm sorry," Payton said in his postgame press conference on Sunday. "If you look it up, in 2008, in a similar situation — even a more radical reverse — fumbled, Tampa Bay beat us. I know better. Every once in a while you fall in love with a play." Contingency Plan Must be Established In the event that Waddle is inactive on Sunday, the Broncos would be down to Courtland Sutton, Marvin Mims, and Troy Franklin as its primary wideouts, with Pat Bryant (ankle) still on short-term injured reserve. home.headline: Is Jaylen Waddle Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Broncos vs. Cardinals in NFL Week 7)
home.blurb: Denver Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle was limited in practice this week with a chest injury before logging a full session on Friday. Jaylen Waddle (chest) said he is good to go for Sunday's game at Arizona after being limited in practice the previous two days. Via @christomasson pic.twitter.com/HxpBUEsUmp Is Jaylen Waddle Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Broncos vs. Cardinals in NFL Week 7) Skip to main content ON SI He's now officially off the injury report and expected to play in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals. Waddle briefly left Denver's Week 6 win on Thursday night against the Seattle Seahawks, but he returned to the game in the second half. The Broncos star had four catches in the win, though the entire Denver passing offense has struggled this season. Bo Nix has not gotten going under center, and it's led to a rather pedestrian stat line for Waddle. He has 38 targets on the season, yet he's turned them into just 22 catches for 228 yards and a score. Waddle also has two carries for 23 yards. Outside of a big Week 2 against Jacksonville (eight catches 138 yards), Waddle has 35 or fewer receiving yards in every other game. Denver traded a first-round pick to Miami for Waddle in the offseason, so at some point the team needs to get him going with Nix at quarterback. This week, the SI Betting team has a player prop for both Nix and Waddle in Sunday's matchup with the two-win Cards. Best Broncos Prop Bet vs. Cardinals in NFL Week 7 Jaylen Waddle Anytime TD (+200) This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shared his favorite props in his Player Prop Countdown column , and he’s targeting Bo Nix to toss multiple touchdown passes. He also shared his favorite props for this game, and he believes Waddle is worth a look to score: Jaylen Waddle has nine more receptions than any other wide receiver on the Denver Broncos, and now he gets to face a Cardinals' defense that's in the bottom 10 in virtually every single pass defense metric. That could lead to big things for Waddle, who is due for another touchdown after having scored just one through his first six games as a Bronco. He's a great bet to score on Sunday at 2-1 odds. home.blurb: After being a limited participant in all three practices ahead of Week 7, cornerback Pat Surtain II (ankle) was listed as a full participant following the Broncos' Wednesday practice. While Surtain improved to a full participant, safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), defensive lineman Zach Allen (hamstring) and wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) did not practice. Hufanga suffered an injury in Denver's Week 5 win over the Chargers and has not played in the Broncos' last two games. Allen and Waddle each played in the Broncos' Week 7 win vs. Arizona. Tackle Garett Bolles (hip) and wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr. (ankle) were limited in Wednesday's practice, while defensive tackle Malcolm Roach (neck) and inside linebacker Karene Reid (elbow) were both listed as full participants. home.headline: Kansas City Chiefs' first injury report for Week 8 vs. Denver Broncos sees some very important players returning to practice
home.blurb: Everyone participated in practice in some capacity on Wednesday, just as Chiefs HC Andy Reid said they would . The team ran a light 10-10-10 practice to start the week before ramping up with pads on Thursday and Friday. Returning to the lineup was WR Rashee Rice, who missed the past two games with a hamstring injury. Additionally, starting RT Jaylon Moore returned after missing Week 7 with a concussion. The other player back at practice? Chiefs second-year DT Omarr Norman-Lott. He was designated to return to practice after missing over 365 days with an ACL injury. KEY: DNP = Did not participate | LP = Limited participation | FP = Full participation | NIR = Not injury related Rashee Rice and Omarr Norman-Lott were both limited on a light practice day. I expect Rice to ramp up a bit more on Thursday, while Norman-Lott will likely ease back in after not practicing for over 12 months. Pat Surtain II's full participation on Wednesday is a positive sign that he'll return to action in Week 8 after missing multiple weeks with an ankle injury. away.headline: Christian Gonzalez on Carlton Davis’ Return: Patriots' Secondary Back at 100% vs. Dolphins
away.blurb: During his press conference this afternoon, Patriots All-Pro cornerback Christian Gonzalez spoke to the media on Davis III’s return on Sunday. “CD is a great vet, somebody that I lean on a lot, able to talk to, pick his mind about certain things. He’s seen a lot of balls, so just having him back out there is amazing.” Gonzalez also expressed his excitement to have all the defensive backs available to play on Sunday. “So, excited to get all of us back. I think this is the first game since the first week [it’s] going to be all of us out there. So, excited for that to get back on the field with all of them.” Now, with the return of Davis III and top backup perimeter cornerbacks in Channing Canada (hamstring) and Karon Prunty (hamstring), Mike Vrabel’s defense will have all of its defensive backs healthy for Sunday’s matchup against the Dolphins. It looks like the extended time off has done the Patriots well in the health department. On Wednesday afternoon, New England released its Week 8 Injury Report for their game against the Miami Dolphins , and it was revealed that the entire secondary practiced in full for the first time in weeks. The most notable name still with an injury designation is Miami native cornerback Carlton Davis III , who has been dealing with a neck injury that he suffered in Week 1. “Yeah, I mean it’s everything,” said Gonzalez. New England’s secondary this season has had to dig deep and rely on depth pieces in Charles Woods and Kindle Vildor, who have stepped up in Davis III’s absence. Through seven weeks, the Patriots’ defensive backs have been in the middle of the pack in both total passing yards (19th) and passing yards per game (15th). For New England, the hope is that the team’s injury woes are behind them as the focus shifts to shutting down the opposing team’s passing offenses for the weeks to come.

away.headline: Patriots injury analysis: Pats get a much-needed reprieve in Week 7
away.blurb: The New England Patriots dropped to 4-3 on the year and out of the current AFC playoff picture with their loss to the Chicago Bears on Thursday night. However, not all was bad: the injury-ravaged team received a much-needed reprieve. S Kevin Byard III: Early in the second quarter, the veteran safety had to be checked out by trainers on the field due to an apparent left shoulder injury. He subsequently jogged off the field under his own power and into the blue medical tent, but reemerged after a brief evaluation. Byard ended up missing just four snaps before his return. He ended the game with a 94% playing time share , not missing any other reps down the stretch. In fact, there were only two noticeable injuries after rewatching the contest. Patriots injury analysis: NFL Week 7 DT Christian Barmore: Barmore made what could have been one of the biggest plays of the game in the late fourth quarter, sacking Caleb Williams for a 10-yard loss. Unfortunately, the play did not end up mattering — kicker Cairo Santos kicked a career-long field goal to effectively ice the game — while the sixth-year defensive tackle remained on the ground afterwards: he had landed awkwardly on his right hand and required medical assistance. Barmore walked off the field and with the Patriots playing no more defensive snaps did not get an opportunity to reenter the game. What this means for the Patriots While the injuries to both Kevin Byard and Christian Barmore could have been potentially concerning, it appears neither will be a long-term issue. Byard returned to the game, while head coach Mike Vrabel said about Barmore on Monday that “he’ll be fine.” Him and Barmore both being present at practice on Monday is concrete proof of that. For the Patriots, especially considering that they were on a short week, this is definitive good news. The team, after all, had at least lost some starters or key reserves to injury in almost every game this season so far. Now heading into a Week 8 contest against the Miami Dolphins off a mini-bye, they seemingly are trending in the right direction again. No major injuries were added on Thursday, while the team is getting healthier — as evidenced by the fact that guard Ben Brown (knee) also was back on the practice fields on Monday. The first injury report of the week will be published on Wednesday afternoon, and give more information about the current state of the team. home.headline: Breaking Down a New Willis Issue and the Two Concussions on the Dolphins' Lengthy Injury Report
home.blurb: Only two players on the active roster missed the first practice ahead of the team's Week 8 game against the New England Patriots, but both rookie guard Kadyn Proctor and cornerback JuJu Brents were out because they're in the concussion protocol. The injury report, though, featured eight players listed as limited participants. The other five players listed as limited were TE Greg Dulcich (ankle), S Michael Taaffe (neck/foot), S Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder), WR Malik Washington (knee) and WR Jared Wayne (knee). Only Trader had an injury reported in the press box Sunday, so it's possible than any of the other four were injured in practice. The most prominent players among those who were limited were wide receiver A.J. Brown (ankle) and starting right tackle Morgan Moses (foot). Breaking Down a New Willis Issue and the Two Concussions on the Dolphins' Lengthy Injury Report Skip to main content SI.COM If the Miami Dolphins are going to make it two in a row after getting their first victory of the season, they might have to overcome some injury issues. Because of the fickle nature of concussions, it's impossible to predict whether either or both will be able to play against the Patriots, and Brents was spotted on the outside practice fields at the Baptist Health Training Complex doing conditioning work, which clearly is a good sign. The first injury report of the week for the Dolphins was a long one with 13 names on it, and a new issue for quarterback Malik Willis. After earlier this season being listed with a toe issue and then with a thumb injury, this time Willis is dealing with a groin injury, although he was a full participant in practice Wednesday. Another full participant was edge defender Rob Beal Jr., who has missed the past four games because of a hamstring injury. On the list was cornerback Reese Taylor, who missed the past three games with a quad injury, and long-snapper Tucker Addington and tight end Will Kacmarek both were on the injury report last week before playing in the 28-25 victory against the New York Jets. Head coach Jeff Hafley revealed the concussions before practice before taking questions from the assembled media. Hafley also indicated that backup Jarrett Kingston would be taking Proctor's reps at left guard during practice. Kingston was the one who replaced Jonah Savaiinaea at right guard after the 2025 second-round pick was injured in the first half of the Week 5 loss at Hard Rock Stadium. Kingston, who obviously is the No. 3 guard on the roster, was claimed off waivers from the Houston Texans after the cuts to 53. That losing skid is a record during the Nick Sirianni era and longest since 2016, when Carson Wentz was a QB prodigy in his rookie season. That was also the season Lane Johnson missed 10 games because of a PED suspension. The Eagles went 2-8 without him. This season, Johnson retired. So far, the Eagles are 0-4 without him. Johnson isn't coming back. Neither is quarterback Jalen Hurts, who's presumably out for the season to treat blood clots that have traveled to both of his lungs. Buy Philadelphia Eagles tickets The Cowboys exposed all of that, including an AWOL defense that couldn't stop the run as the Cowboys rushed for 204 yards, or pass as Dak Prescott threw for 212 yards and three touchdowns. But there were positives that the Eagles can build on heading into their Nov. 1 matchup against the Commanders . The game between the 2-5 Eagles and the 1-4-1 Commanders is the Sunday Night Football game. This probably won't be a ratings bonanza. Unless, of course, viewers like watching two teams battle it out for the opposite of NFC East supremacy. The Eagles won the first game 24-22 in the season opener on Sept. 13. Still, the Eagles' offense had perhaps its best game, or at least its best 2½ quarters, of the season. Another division loss would make an already difficult climb even steeper for a team that's more realistically already on to 2027 due to so many key injuries. 2. Keep an eye on Saquon: Speaking of injuries, Saquon Barkley played only nine snaps Monday while dealing with hamstring and back issues. He offered an encouraging assessment of his hamstring and said he doesn't expect the back problem to keep him out. His practice workload still warrants watching. 3. The preparation advantage favors Washington: The Commanders come off their bye, while the Eagles turn around from Monday night for a Sunday road game. That's valuable extra time to prepare for Tanner McKee and the Eagles' reshuffled offense. 4. McKee needs help from his defense: Philadelphia's quarterback threw for 211 yards, one touchdown and one interception against Dallas. The Eagles produced three touchdown drives, but their defense couldn't slow the Cowboys. Sustaining drives only helps so much if the other team keeps answering. 5. We should expect points: With a game total around 40.5, we're not asking for much to hit 41 points, even from these two offenses. The trends are on our side. Commanders coach Dan Quinn is 8-1 to the over in division games since the start of last season, while the Eagles are 7-1 to the over against the Commanders under coach Nick Sirianni. Tanner McKee can keep things functional when the Eagles protect him and stay balanced. That becomes much harder if the Commanders take away the run and force longer passing situations. The ever-forgiving NFC East could keep the Eagles afloat for a bit, but they need to score a win against the Dallas Cowboys on Monday night to keep pace in a wide-open division. The official word on Barkley is expected closer to game time, but all signs are pointing towards the Pro Bowler making his official return in Week 7. The Eagles listed Barkley as questionable but he did practice in full on Saturday, with NFL Network's Ian Rapoport noting that the expectation is for Barkley to take the field on Monday. The fact that this is a Monday night game without a clear call makes life quite difficult for managers with Barkley on their roster. The upside that Barkley offers is enormous, but if he is ruled out prior to the game there are few legitimate alternatives to plug in for him. The good news for Barkley backers is that the Eagles will likely give him everything he can handle if he's active. Both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks are out for this game, leaving Dallas Goedert and Makai Lemon as the top receiving weapons for backup QB Tanner McKee.
