away.headline: Eagles face running back emergency after Dameon Pierce lands on injured reserve
away.blurb: With three other running backs already on the list and Saquon Barkley dealing with multiple injuries, Philadelphia could enter its Week 8 matchup against the Washington Commanders with extremely limited options. The situation is particularly concerning because Barkley, the team's established starter, is also dealing with hamstring and back problems. He returned against Dallas after missing time with a hamstring injury but played only 10 snaps before his back forced him out of the game. Barkley said he expected to be available against Washington, but his participation remains a key storyline heading into Sunday night. Philadelphia cannot afford to assume its star running back will be able to handle his usual workload. With Pierce unavailable, Philadelphia must consider how to distribute its carries if Barkley cannot play or remains limited. The Philadelphia Eagles are facing a growing problem in their backfield after placing Dameon Pierce on injured reserve. Pierce was placed on injured reserve Wednesday after leaving the Eagles' 38-21 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. He joins Tank Bigsby, Will Shipley and Carson Steele, leaving four Philadelphia running backs on injured reserve. Eagles could turn to Elijah Mitchell and Jaydon Blue Elijah Mitchell is one potential option. The veteran signed with the Eagles practice squad earlier in October and was elevated for the Dallas game, recording three carries for 11 yards. Jaydon Blue, meanwhile, was signed from the practice squad to the active roster on Wednesday. Both backs could receive opportunities against Washington, although Mitchell's availability depends on Philadelphia's roster decisions before kickoff. Neither player offers the same established role as Barkley, leaving the coaching staff with difficult decisions about how to structure the offense. The Eagles' ground game has already struggled this season. Philadelphia entered Week 8 ranked 27th in the NFL with 88 rushing yards per game and 24th with 3.9 yards per carry. Those numbers make the injuries even more damaging. The team is not simply losing depth from an otherwise productive rushing attack; it must find a way to improve its ground production while potentially relying on less experienced options. Philadelphia must find another way to support its offense The Eagles' immediate priority is determining Barkley's status and establishing a workable backfield rotation. If he cannot handle a full workload, Philadelphia may need to lean more heavily on its passing game and use shorter throws or additional personnel to compensate for the shortage of running backs. That adjustment would place more responsibility on the remaining offensive playmakers and the coaching staff. It could also make the offense more predictable if Washington can anticipate when Philadelphia is likely to run or pass. away.blurb: Dallas Goedert is good to go for Monday, while Saquon Barkley and Jalyx Hunt inch closer to a potential return. "It's just kind of the same injury that I sustained earlier. I just had a little bit of inflammation in there, had to let that settle down, but felt really good running out there today," Goedert said after Saturday's practice. "I want to be out there anytime I can. We only get 17 games. To miss a game, to miss two games, it always stinks. So if I can be available, I'm going to do everything I can to play. "I'm going to go out there and do whatever I can to help the team win, whether it's run blocking, pass blocking, or hopefully get a couple catches. "It's definitely a big opportunity with the team," Lemon said. "I'm just super excited to go out there with the guys, put on a good performance. Had a great week of practice with all the guys. home.headline: Eagles Week 8 injury report: 6 players listed as DNP ahead of Commanders game
home.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles opened their Week 8 preparations Wednesday with an extensive injury report, listing six players as nonparticipants and another six as limited participants ahead of Sunday's NFC East matchup against the Washington Commanders . Barkley's status remains one of the biggest concerns after the veteran suffered a back injury during Monday night's 38-21 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. The Eagles listed him with hamstring and back injuries Wednesday, adding another concern for a player who recently returned from a hamstring issue that kept him out of consecutive games. Barkley opened the Dallas matchup with a 29-yard run and scored a touchdown on Philadelphia's first possession, but his workload was limited after his back tightened. He eventually left the game, forcing the Eagles to rely on their remaining running backs. Lemon responded with his first career touchdown reception against the Cowboys, but the Eagles would benefit from having additional receiving options available against Washington. Campbell was listed as a nonparticipant with hamstring and quadriceps injuries, adding to concerns for a defense that struggled against Dallas. Jones was sidelined by a hamstring injury, while Covey was listed with a knee injury after leaving Monday night's game. The defensive injury situation extends beyond those six players. Outside linebackers Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt and Nolan Smith were all listed as limited participants, along with defensive backs Michael Carter II, linebacker Smael Mondon Jr. and defensive tackle Moro Ojomo. The Eagles return to practice Thursday, and actual participation should better indicate which players are progressing toward Sunday's game. Philadelphia held a walkthrough rather than a traditional practice, so Wednesday's injury report estimated how players would have participated in a full session. The report included 19 players, with running back Saquon Barkley, wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, linebacker Jihaad Campbell, wide receiver Britain Covey, and cornerback Jonathan Jones all listed as nonparticipants. The injury comes at a difficult time for Philadelphia, which has lost five straight games and struggled to produce consistently on offense. Barkley's availability will be particularly important against Washington as the Eagles attempt to establish a balanced offense with Tanner McKee under center. Philadelphia's receiving corps also remains a concern. Smith was listed as a nonparticipant because of a hamstring injury, while Wicks continues to deal with an ankle injury. Both receivers missed Monday night's loss to Dallas, leaving rookie Makai Lemon and the team's remaining pass catchers to handle expanded responsibilities. Greenard continues to deal with an ankle injury, while Hunt was listed with knee and ankle injuries. home.headline: Eagles-Commanders Week 8 injury report, with analysis
home.blurb: • Unsurprisingly, Saquon Barkley was listed with a DNP after he struggled to stay on the field last Monday night against the Cowboys. • The Eagles are getting healthier on the edge, as Jalyx Hunt, Nolan Smith, and Jonathan Greenard were all limited participants. • QB Jalen Hurts (IR, season over) : Hurts is out indefinitely with blood clots in his lungs. Tanner McKee has taken over as the team's starting quarterback. • RB Tank Bigsby (IR, eligible to return after Week 8) : Bigsby suffered an injury Week 4 against the Rams that required core muscle surgery. He will likely return this season, but could miss up to two months. • RB Will Shipley (IR, eligible to return after Week 9) : Shipley suffered a Lisfranc injury and will be out a while. Shipley is the Eagles' best RB in pass protection, but he only has 57 yards on 20 carries this season. • RB Dameon Pierce (IR, eligible to return after Week 12) : The Eagles' top four RBs are all injured. • The Commanders have a bunch of guys on injured reserve (below), but the only two names of note who did not practice on Wednesday were WR Stefon Diggs and DT Javon Kinlaw. • LT Laremy Tunsil (IR) : During training camp, Tunsil tore his triceps and will be out for a chunk of the regular season. He is arguably the best player on Commanders' roster. The Commanders didn't have much in the way of ideal replacements. They settled on Brandon Coleman, who was in a camp battle with Chris Paul for the starting LG spot. Coleman started 12 games for the Commanders at LT in 2024. He also started three games at LT when Tunsil got hurt last season. Massive downgrade. So far in 2026, PFF has Coleman down for 4 sacks allowed. • RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt : Croskey-Merritt is the Commanders' RB1. He had a good rookie season as a runner, carrying 175 times for 805 yards (4.6 YPC) and 8 TDs. However, he also had fumbling issues and was not a threat as a receiver. In 2026, he carried 67 times for 239 yards (3.6 YPC) and 2 TDs before landing on IR with a groin injury. With Croskey-Merritt out, Rachaad White is the Commanders' lead back, with Jeremy McNichols working in as well. home.blurb: Three Injured Washington Commanders Return to Practice CommandersRoundtable 141 Members • 1,206 Posts CommandersRoundtable CommandersRoundtable Related stories Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Three Injured Washington Commanders Return to Practice Ahmed Ghafir Partner Oct 26, 2026 6:22 PM Published Oct 26, 2026 6:22 PM Updated Oct 26, 2026 6:43 PM Defensive end Charles Omenihu is one of three players the Washington Commanders saw return to practice on Monday ahead of the week eight primetime meeting against the Philadelphia Eagles Head coach Dan Quinn noted that quarterback Marcus Mariota and defensive end Charles Omenihu will return to practice on Monday. The veteran quarterback went down in the week four loss against the Indianapolis Colts in London with what the team described as a knee injury, allowing rookie Athan Kaliakmanis to make his NFL debut after replacing him before Mariota avoided injury reserve. Omenihu has missed the last two games with a groin/ankle injury, marking a welcomed return for the defensive line's depth. Yet there was some bad news after Quinn revealed defensive tackle Javon Kinlaw remains sidelined as head coach Dan Quinn noted his recovery has not materialized as hoped. Kinlaw has battled through injuries in his second season with the franchise despite not missing any games yet, though whether he will ultimately be available in week eight remains to be seen. On the flip side, how healthy the Eagles are in week eight remains to be seen with defensive back Michael Carter, wide receiver DeVonta Smith, outside linebacker Nolan Smith and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks all ruled out for the Monday night matchup against the Dallas Cowboys in week seven. That doesn't include running back Saquon Barkley among the over dozen of Eagles who drew the questionable tag in the latest injury report, while head coach Nick Sirianni is still battling through the sudden retirement of All-Pro offensive tackle Lane Johnson. Quarterback Tanner McKee is also set to start in week seven with Jalen Hurts sidelined for the remainder of the season. More Videos The Washington Commanders are fresh off the bye week and will shift their attention toward the second consecutive primetime game with a home game against the Philadelphia Eagles set for week eight. The Commanders will also enter the divisional game a bit more healthy, too. Quinn also noted that wide receiver Treylon Burks, who left the week six loss in the closing minutes due to injury, will also work his way back into practice with a chance to elevate the unit's depth. Burks will loom large as head coach Dan Quinn noted that it will be the rest of the Commanders' wide receivers who will be asked to step up to mitigate the season-ending loss of veteran Terry McLaurin . Also, the Dolphins have plenty of confidence after beating the Jets last week, and this offense is a lot better with rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas, who contributed two catches for 70 yards and two touchdowns in his first game since sustaining an ankle injury in Week 2. Peter Dewey Week 8 Upset Pick Atlanta Falcons (+114) vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers The Falcons may be the most confusing team in the NFL, but I think their best version is the top squad in the NFC South. I’m buying Atlanta as a road underdog against a Tampa Bay team that is 0-4 against the spread at home and potentially overvalued after a Week 7 rout of the Carolina Panthers. Baker Mayfield (thumb) wasn’t asked to do much, but the Bucs beat up a Carolina defense that has allowed the most yards per carry in the NFL. That won’t be the case against Atlanta, which is No. 4 in EPA/Rush and 12th in opponent yards per play in 2026. Tampa Bay has been great defensively as well (third in EPA/Play, seventh in yards per play), but the offensive upside is capped with Mayfield and Emeka Egbuka banged up. Plus, this Falcons offense has been much better with Michael Penix Jr. under center over the last few weeks. The Falcons are 3-2 when Penix starts, and I love this price against a Tampa Bay team with clear flaws and a quarterback at less than 100 percent. Iain MacMillan Week 8 Upset Pick Chicago Bears (+140) vs. Seattle Seahawks I'm ready to believe in the Chicago Bears. Ben Johnson is clearly the real deal as head coach, and Caleb Williams has improved significantly since last season. Last season, he ranked 39th out of 45 starting quarterbacks in completion percentage over expected. This season, he ranks first at +9.0%. The Bears' defense has also been better than people expected this season, ranking fourth in the NFL in opponent success rate. I still have some concerns surrounding the Seattle offense. It did enough to beat the Chiefs last week, but their running game is still weak, and Sam Darnold hasn't been as efficient as he was a year ago. I'll take the Bears as my upset pick of the week. picks.blurb: Bears vs. Seahawks bold predictions for Week 8 Monday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers win World Series Milwaukee can finally celebrate Dybantsa delivers in NBA debut WNBA Finals fatigue Jokić's 200th triple-double Bears vs. Seahawks bold predictions for Week 8 Monday Night Football Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints Wed, October 28, 2026 at 11:24 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Chicago Bears have demonstrated quite a bit of explosiveness this season, especially when Caleb Williams is under center and running back Kyle Monangai is healthy and in the lineup. Williams has been in the lineup for the past two games and has demonstrated no ill effects from the hamstring injury that sidelined him earlier in the year. Monangai has missed the last three games and while he is improving, there are no guarantees that he will be back in the lineup for this game. The Seahawks have not been at their best in the first half of the season and they take a 4-3 record into this home game. They are coming off a key Sunday night victory over the Kansas City Chiefs in which their defense performed at a peak level. They will need that kind of effort against the Bears. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Sam Darnold was one of the keys to Seattle's surge to last year's Super Bowl title. He has not been as efficient this season, as interceptions have been an issue. The Bears defense got a huge lift from their ability to create takeaways last year. They have not been as proficient in that area this season — minus-1 on the takeaway/turnover table — but they have been a middle-of-the-pack defense that has been moderately capable this season. This game could come down to turnover differential, and if the Bears are going to win on the road, they have to gain an advantage in this area. Williams will throw for 250 yards and 2 TDs Williams has demonstrated that he can rise to the occasion and handle pressure. He has an excellent partnership with head coach Ben Johnson, and it appears that those two will allow the Bears to remain contenders in the division and the NFC for several years. Williams has all the tools that an outstanding quarterback needs, and as the No. 1 selection in the 2024 NFL Draft, nearly all scouts and personnel specialists were predicting great things for him. However, Williams struggled in his rookie season under former head coach Matt Eberflus. That coach did not have the wherewithal to teach and demand outstanding play from Williams. However that changed under Johnson, and the quarterback reads and understands defenses, and he knows how to pick apart good defenses and make key plays. The one area that scouts did not get right about Williams was his speed and escapability from the pocket. He was thought to be above average or good in that area, and that assessment did not give him enough credit. He is sensational in that area. He has a strong partnership with wide receivers Rome Odunze and Luther Burden, as well as big-play tight end Colston Loveland. This trio should be able to cause problems for the Seattle defense, which is one of the strongest units in the league. Williams and the receivers will not overpower the Seahawks defense, but the quarterback will throw 2 TD passes and approach the 275-yard mark. Smith-Njigba is unstoppable, will exceed 125 yards and score a TD Mandatory Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images The Bears regularly have to contend with outstanding receivers like Justin Jefferson, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Christian Watson in the NFC North. However, Seattle wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba is at another level. He is coming off a sensational game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Smith-Njigba was targeted 12 times by Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold and he caught 9 passes for 150 yards and 1 touchdown. The Chiefs knew he was the central point of the Seattle offensive game plan, yet defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo could not do anything to slow him down. Stopping him was out of the question. Chicago defensive coordinator Dennis Allen will face the same issue. Allen certainly knows what it is like to face outstanding wideouts in the NFC North, but Smith-Njigba may be too strong for the Bears defense. He has caught 58 passes for 867 yards and 8 TDs, and asking CBs Jaylon Johnson, Malik Muhammad and Kyler Gordon to prevent him from making big plays will be folly. The best way for the Bears to go about it would be pressuring Darnold and keep him from delivering accurate passes. The Bears have registered 19 sacks and Darnold has been trapped 14 times thus far. Allen's top priority will be to make sure his personnel gets in Darnold's face and prevents him from getting the ball to Smith-Njigba. That scenario is unlikely, but it is Chicago's best defensive hope. Bold game prediction: Seahawks 27, Bears 24 The Bears have the weapons to go into Seattle and give the defending champions a battle for 60 minutes. This is the kind of game that Johnson and Williams would like to use as a measuring stick. However, the Seahawks have already lost 3 games and they can't afford to lose any more. They will have a major challenge chasing down the 49ers in the NFC West, and dropping a home game to a solid team is not in their plans. The Seahawks played their best all-around game against the Chiefs in Week 7, and they will stay on track against the Bears. Seattle wins a close, well-played game against Williams and the Bears.
